56:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Waqi'ah Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I have grown old. He said: Hud, Al-Waqi’ah, Al-Mursalat, ‘Amma Yatas’alun, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my hair turn grey. Narrated by At-Tirmidhi who said: Hasan Gharib. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said in the biography of Abdullah bin Mas’ud on the authority of Amr bin Ar-Rabi’ bin Tariq Al-Masry: Al-Sari bin Yahya Ash-Shaibani narrated to us on the authority of Abu Shuja’ on the authority of Abu Dhabiya who said: Abdullah fell ill with the illness from which he died. Uthman bin Affan visited him and said: What do you complain of? He said: My sins. He said: What do you desire? He said: The mercy of my Lord. He said: Shall I not order a doctor for you? He said: The doctor made me sick. He said: Shall I not order a stipend for you? He said: I have no need for it. He said: It will be for your daughters after you. He said: Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I ordered my daughters to recite Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night, for I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night, poverty will never befall him. Then Ibn Asakir said: This is what he said. The correct version is from Shuja’ as narrated by Abdullah ibn Wahb from As-Sari. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: As-Sari ibn Yahya told me that Shuja’ told him on the authority of Abu Dhubayah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night, poverty will never befall him. So Abu Dhubayah never abandoned it. Abu Ya’la narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim on the authority of Muhammad ibn Munib on the authority of As-Sari ibn Yahya on the authority of Shuja’ on the authority of Abu Dhubayah on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud with this chain of transmission. Then Abu Ya’la narrated it on the authority of Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il on the authority of Muhammad bin Munib Al-Adani on the authority of Al-Sari bin Yahya on the authority of Abu Dhubayah on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night, poverty will never befall him. He did not mention Shuja’ in his Musnad, who said: I have commanded my daughters to recite it every night. Ibn Asakir also narrated it on the authority of Hajjaj bin Nusayr and Uthman bin Al-Yaman on the authority of Al-Sari bin Yahya on the authority of Shuja’ on the authority of Abu Fatimah, who said: Abdullah fell ill, so Uthman bin Affan came to visit him. He mentioned the hadith in full. Uthman bin Al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client of Ali bin Abi Talib. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Isra’il and Yahya ibn Adam told us, Isra’il told us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray prayers similar to the prayers you pray today, but he would shorten them, and his prayer was shorter than your prayer. And he would recite al-Waqi’ah and similar surahs in the dawn prayer. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Al-Waqi’ah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was given this name because of its being and existence, as God the Almighty said: Then on that Day the Event will occur. God the Almighty said: Its occurrence will not be false. That is, if God wills it to occur, there will be no one to avert it or repel it. As He said: Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from God for which there is no repelling. And He said: A questioner asked about a punishment to befall * the disbelievers, which can be averted. And God the Almighty said: “And the Day He says, ‘Be,’ and it is. His word is the truth, and His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.” The meaning of false, as Muhammad ibn Ka’b said, is that it must be. Qatadah said: There is no duality, apostasy, or return in it. Ibn Jarir said: The false is a verbal noun like the consequence and well-being. God the Almighty says: lowering and raising meaning that it lowers some people to the lowest of the low, to Hellfire, even if they were honored in this world, and raises others to the highest of the high, to eternal bliss, even if they were lowly in this world. This is what Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yazid bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Mus’ab Al-Ma’ni told us, Humaid bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Ru’asi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: lowering and raising It lowers some people and raises others. Ubaidullah Al-Ataki said, on the authority of Uthman bin Suraqah, the cousin of Umar bin Al-Khattab: lowering and raising He said: The Hour will lower the enemies of God to Hellfire and raise the friends of God to Paradise. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It lowers men who were exalted in this world, and raises men who were humble in this world. Al-Suddi said: It lowers the arrogant and raises the humble. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: lowering and raising means: It makes the near and the far hear. Ikrimah said: It lowers so that the nearest hear, and it raises so that the farthest hear. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said the same. God the Almighty said: {When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking} meaning it is moved with a shaking, trembling and shaking throughout its length and breadth. For this reason, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said regarding God the Almighty’s statement: {When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking} that is, it is shaken with a severe earthquake. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It shakes with what is in it like a sieve is shaken with what is in it. This is like God the Almighty’s statement: {When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake}. God the Almighty said: {O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing.}. God the Almighty said: {And the mountains will be ground down} meaning they will be crumbled to pieces. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and others. Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become as God the Almighty said: {a heap of sand}. God the Almighty said: {And it was like scattered dust} Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Harith on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: Scattered dust is like dust that shines and then disappears and nothing of it remains. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And it was like scattered dust means the dust that flies from a fire when it is blazing, sparks fly from it, but when it falls, it is nothing. Ikrimah said: Scattered dust is that which the wind has scattered and dispersed. Qatada said: Scattered dust is like the downy trees that the winds scatter. This verse, like its sisters, indicates that the mountains will move from their places on the Day of Resurrection, and will be removed, moved, blown away, and become like carded wool. God Almighty says: And you were three groups meaning that people will be divided into three groups on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a group on the right of the Throne. They are the ones who came out of the right side of Adam, and they will be given their books in their right hands and will be taken to the right. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise, and others are on the left of the Throne, and they are the ones who came out of the left side of Adam, and they will be given their books in their left hands and will be taken to the left. They are the majority of the people of Hell - may God protect us from their actions - and a group will be foremost before Him, the Almighty, and they are more special, more fortunate, and closer to the people of the right, who are their masters. Among them are the Messengers, Prophets, Truthful Ones, and Martyrs. They are fewer in number than the people of the right, and for this reason God Almighty said: So the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? And the foremost - what are the foremost. Thus He divided them into these three types at the end of the Surah at the time of their death. Thus He mentioned them in His saying, the Almighty: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, and among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of God.” This is according to one of the two opinions regarding the one who wrongs himself, as explained above. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Jabir al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And you were three mates, he said: It is the one in Surat al-Mala'ikah, "Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds." Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: These three mates are the ones mentioned at the end of the surah and in Surat al-Mala'ikah. Yazid al-Ruqashi said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, And you were three mates, he said: Three types. Mujahid said: And you were three mates, meaning three groups. Maymun ibn Mihran said: Three groups. Ubaydullah al-'Atki said, on the authority of Uthman ibn Suraqah, the cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: And you were three mates, two in Paradise and one in Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when souls are paired, he said: The pairs, each man from each people who used to do his work, and that is because God Almighty says: “And you will be three pairs. * So the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” He said: They are the pairs. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna told us, al-Bara’ al-Ghanawi told us, al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: And the companions of the right - who are the companions of the right? and The companions of the left - who are the companions of the left? Then he took two handfuls of food in his hand and said: This is for Paradise, and I do not care, and this is for Hell, and I do not care. Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran told us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: Do you know who will be the first to enter the shade of God on the Day of Resurrection? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Those who, when given the truth, accept it, and when asked, give it up, and judge for the people as they judge for themselves. Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Abu Harzah, and Ya’qub ibn Mujahid said: And the foremost, the foremost are the prophets, peace be upon them. Al-Suddi said: They are the people of the highest heavens. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the foremost, the foremost. He said: Joshua bin Nun, he went before Moses, and the believer of the family of Yasin, he went before Jesus, and Ali bin Abi Talib went before Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Muhammad bin Harun al-Fallas on the authority of Abdullah bin Ismail al-Madaini al-Bazzar, on the authority of Shuaib bin al-Dahhak al-Madaini on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said, and he mentioned on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Qurrah, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: And the foremost are the foremost are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Kharijah with it. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: And the foremost are the foremost meaning from every nation. Al-Awza’i said on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sawdah that he recited this verse: And the foremost are the foremost * Those are the ones brought near then he said: The first of them to go to the mosque and the first of them to go out in the cause of God. All of these sayings are correct, because what is meant by the foremost are those who hasten to do good deeds as they have been commanded, as God the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth and God the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth and He said: “Whoever is foremost in this world and is the first to do good will be among the foremost to receive honor in the Hereafter, because the reward is of the same kind as the deed, and as you judge, you will be judged. For this reason God the Almighty said: “Those are the ones brought near * In Gardens of Delight.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Yahya bin Zakariya Al-Fazari Al-Razi told us: Kharijah bin Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The angels said: O Lord, You have given the world to the children of Adam, so they eat, drink and marry, so give us the Hereafter. He said: I will not do that. So they went back three times, and He said: I will not make the one I created with My hands like the one to whom I said, Be, and he was. Then Abdullah recited: “And the foremost will be the foremost. Those will be the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight.” This narration was narrated by Imam Uthman bin Sa`id Al-Darimi in his book, Al-Radd `ala Al-Jahmiyyah, and its wording is: Then God the Almighty said: I will not make the righteous offspring of the one I created with My hands like the one to whom I said, Be, and he was.

God the Almighty said: {And the mountains will be ground down} meaning they will be crumbled to pieces. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and others. Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become as God the Almighty said: {a heap of sand}. God the Almighty said: {And it was like scattered dust} Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Harith on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: Scattered dust is like dust that shines and then disappears and nothing of it remains. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And it was like scattered dust means the dust that flies from a fire when it is blazing, sparks fly from it, but when it falls, it is nothing. Ikrimah said: Scattered dust is that which the wind has scattered and dispersed. Qatada said: Scattered dust is like the downy trees that the winds scatter. This verse, like its sisters, indicates that the mountains will move from their places on the Day of Resurrection, and will be removed, moved, blown away, and become like carded wool. They are the ones who came out of the right side of Adam, and they will be given their books in their right hands and will be taken to the right. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise, and others are on the left of the Throne, and they are the ones who came out of the left side of Adam, and they will be given their books in their left hands and will be taken to the left. Among them are the Messengers, Prophets, Truthful Ones, and Martyrs. They are fewer in number than the people of the right, and for this reason God Almighty said: So the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds." Yazid al-Ruqashi said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, And you were three mates, he said: Three types. Mujahid said: And you were three mates, meaning three groups. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna told us, al-Bara’ al-Ghanawi told us, al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: And the companions of the right - who are the companions of the right? and The companions of the left - who are the companions of the left? Then he took two handfuls of food in his hand and said: This is for Paradise, and I do not care, and this is for Hell, and I do not care. Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran told us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: Do you know who will be the first to enter the shade of God on the Day of Resurrection? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Those who, when given the truth, accept it, and when asked, give it up, and judge for the people as they judge for themselves. Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Abu Harzah, and Ya’qub ibn Mujahid said: And the foremost, the foremost are the prophets, peace be upon them. Al-Suddi said: They are the people of the highest heavens. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the foremost, the foremost. He said: Joshua bin Nun, he went before Moses, and the believer of the family of Yasin, he went before Jesus, and Ali bin Abi Talib went before Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Kharijah with it. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: And the foremost are the foremost meaning from every nation. All of these sayings are correct, because what is meant by the foremost are those who hasten to do good deeds as they have been commanded, as God the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth and God the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth and He said: “Whoever is foremost in this world and is the first to do good will be among the foremost to receive honor in the Hereafter, because the reward is of the same kind as the deed, and as you judge, you will be judged. 56:13: God Almighty says, informing us about these forerunners who are brought near, that they are a group, that is, a group of the first ones and a few of the last ones. They differed about what is meant by His saying the first ones and the last ones. It was said that what is meant by the first ones are the past nations and by the last ones is this nation. This is a narration from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, narrated from them by Ibn Abi Hatim. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and he took as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the last ones who will be forerunners on the Day of Resurrection. He did not narrate anything else or attribute it to anyone. What is taken as evidence for this saying is what Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Muhammad Ibn Isa Ibn Al-Tabba’ told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the verse A group of the first ones * A few of the last ones was revealed, this was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise or…” Half of the people of Paradise and you will share the other half. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aswad bin Amir on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Muhammad the seller of silk on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it. A hadith similar to this was narrated from Jabir, and it was narrated by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir on the authority of Hisham bin Amara, who said: Abd Rabbih bin Salih told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the verse When the Event occurs was revealed, it mentioned a group of the former peoples and a few of the latter peoples. Umar said: O Messenger of God, a group of the former peoples and a few of us? He said: So he held off for a year at the end of the surah, then the verse, A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Umar, come and listen to what God has revealed: ‘A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones.’ Beware, from Adam to me there is a group, and my nation is a group, and we will not complete our third until we seek help from the black camel herders who testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.” This is how he included it in the biography of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, in both chain of transmission and text, but its chain of transmission is questionable. Many different chains of transmission have been narrated with the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, the hadith in full, and it is alone in describing Paradise, praise and thanks be to God. What Ibn Jarir chose here is questionable, rather it is a weak statement, because this nation is the best of nations according to the text of the Qur’an. It is unlikely that those who are brought near among others would be more than it, unless the sum of the nations is compared to this nation. It appears that those who are brought near among these people are more than all other nations, and God knows best. The second statement in this regard is the most correct, which is that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: A group of the former peoples means from the beginning of this nation, and a few of the latter peoples means from this nation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan told us, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Muzani told us, I heard Al-Hasan come to this verse, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” He said: As for the foremost, they have passed away, but O God, make us among the people of the right hand. Then he said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told us, he said: al-Hasan recited, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight. A company from the former peoples.” He said, A company from those who have passed away from this nation. My father told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said about this verse, “A company from the former peoples. And a few from the later peoples.” He said: They used to say, or hope, that they were all from this nation. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they were all from this nation. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than the last of it. So it is possible that the verse includes all nations, each nation according to its own circumstances. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahihs and other books from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The best of generations is my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. The hadith in full. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman told us, Ziyad Abu Umar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of my nation is like rain; it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better. This hadith, after determining the authenticity of its chain of transmission, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion is in need of the first of the nation to convey it to those who come after them, it is also in need of those who establish it at the end of it and to establish people upon the Sunnah, narrate it and make it known. The advantage is for the one who comes first. Likewise, the crops are in need of the first rain and the second rain, but the greater foundation is on the first and the crops’ need for it is more pressing, for were it not for it, it would not grow in the earth nor would its foundation be attached to it. For this reason, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. In another version: Until the command of God Almighty comes and they are like that. The point is that this nation is more noble than all other nations, and those who are close to God are more numerous than others and of a higher status due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason, it has been proven by continuous transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said, In this nation there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable. In another version, he said, With every thousand there will be seventy thousand. In another version, he said, With every one there will be seventy thousand. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham bin Yazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam - meaning Ibn Zur’ah - told me, on the authority of Shuraih - meaning Ibn Ubayd - on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a group like a black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say, ‘When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, more came than what came with the prophets, peace be upon them.’” It is good to mention here, when God Almighty says: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones, the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah, where he said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, Abu Amr bin Matar told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Mustafad al-Faryabi told us, Abu Wahb al-Walid bin Abdul Malik bin Ubayd God bin Masrah al-Harrani told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ al-Qurashi al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Zamil. Al-Juhani, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he would say while standing on his two feet, “Glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance,” seventy times. Then he would say, “Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in one day exceed seven hundred.” Then he would say that twice, then face the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be amazed by the vision and then say, Has any of you seen anything? Abu Zamil said: I said, O Messenger of God! He said, “Good you will encounter and evil you will avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Tell me your dream.” I said, “I saw all the people on a wide, easy, pleasant road, and the people were walking on the main road. While they were like that, the road passed by a meadow the likes of which my eyes had never seen before. It was flowing and its water dripped with various types of grass. He said, “It is as if I see the first group of people, when they reached the meadow, saying, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, not turning to the right or to the left.” He said, “It is as if I see them walking on. Then the second group came, and they were many times more numerous than them. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, some of them grazing and some of them taking small handfuls of food. They continued on like that.” He said, “Then the majority of the people came forward. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ and they said, ‘This is the best home.’ It is as if I see them turning to the right and to the left. When I saw that, I stuck to the road until I came to…” The furthest part of the meadow, and behold, O Messenger of God, I see you on a pulpit with seven steps, and you are on the highest step. And behold, to your right is a dark-skinned man with a hooked nose. When he speaks, he soars high that he surpasses the men in height. And behold, to your left is a man with a medium build, a large hawk, with a very handsome face, as if his hair had been bathed in water. When he speaks, you listen in respect of him. And behold, in front of him is an old man who most resembles you in appearance and face. All of you turn to him, seeking him. And behold, in front of him is a lean, lean she-camel. And behold, O Messenger of God, it is as if you are sending her forth. He said: The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned pale for a moment, then he was relieved, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for what you saw of the easy, spacious, and pleasant path, that is what I have carried you upon of guidance and you are upon it. As for the meadow that you saw, it is the world and the treachery of its life. I and my companions proceeded without clinging to anything from it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not return to it, and it did not return to us. Then the second group came after us, and they were many times more than us. Some of them graze and some take the handful, and they were saved on that. Then the majority of the people came and turned in the meadow to the right and to the left. So we belong to God, and to Him we shall return. As for you, you proceeded on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be on it until you meet me. As for the pulpit on which you saw seven steps, and I was at the highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am at the last of them for a thousand. As for the man whom you saw on my right, the thin-skinned one, that is Moses, peace be upon him. When he spoke, he rose above the men by virtue of God’s speech to him. And the one I saw on my left was the four-headed falcon, with many horses, as if his hair had been bathed in water. That is Jesus, son of Mary. We honor him because God honored him. As for the old man whom you saw most similar to me in appearance and face, that is our father Abraham. We all follow his example and imitate him. As for the she-camel that you saw and that you saw me sending, it is the Hour that will come upon us. There will be no prophet after me and no nation after my nation. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not asked about a vision after this except that a man would come and tell him about it voluntarily. God the Almighty said: “On couches adorned with gold.” Ibn Abbas said: meaning woven with gold, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Zaid bin Aslam, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. As-Suddi said: adorned with gold and pearls. Ikrimah said: adorned with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this the camel’s belly is called wadin, which is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul because it is braided. Likewise, the couches in Paradise are braided with gold and pearls. God the Almighty says: {Reclining on them, facing each other} meaning, their faces to each other, with no one behind the other. {Immortal youths will circulate around them} meaning, immortal in one condition, they will not be arrogant about it, they will not grow old, and they will not change. {With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring}. The goblets are the cups that have no spouts or ears, and the pitchers are the ones that combine the two descriptions, and the goblets are the ones that are drunk, and all of them are from wine from a flowing spring, not from vessels that stop and empty, but from gushing springs. God the Almighty says: {They will not suffer from headaches therefrom, nor will they lose their minds, rather they will be stable despite the intense, intoxicating pleasure and achieved pleasure. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There are four characteristics of wine: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urine. So God the Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and exonerated it from these characteristics. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Atiyah, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said, They do not suffer from headaches because of it, meaning they do not have a headache because of it. They said about His statement, nor are they intoxicated, meaning they do not lose their minds. And the Almighty said: And fruits of whatever they choose, and the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire. That is, they will be given whatever fruits they choose. This verse is evidence of the permissibility of eating fruits as they choose. This is indicated by the hadith of ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, which was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad. Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid Al-Tarsi told us, Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl ibn Abd Al-Malik ibn Abi Suwayyah told us, Ubayd God ibn ‘Ukrash told us, on the authority of his father, ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, who said: He once sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the alms tax on their wealth. I arrived in Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajireen and Ansar, and camels came to him that were like the roots of the Arta tree. He said, Who is this man? I said: Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb. He said: Raise your lineage. So I traced my lineage back to Murrah ibn Ubayd, and this is the charity of Murrah ibn Ubayd. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled and said: These are the camels of my people, these are the charity camels of my people. Then he ordered them to be branded with the brand of the charity camels and gathered with them. Then he took my hand and we set off to the house of Umm Salamah. He said: Is there any food? We were brought a large bowl-like dish full of tharid and flour, and he started eating from it. I started to beat its sides with my hand, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grabbed my right hand with his left hand and said: O Ukrash, eat from one place, for it is one food. Then a plate was brought to us containing dates or fresh dates. Ubaydullah was uncertain whether it was fresh dates or dried dates. I started to eat from what was in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) moved around in the plate and he said: O Ukrash, eat from wherever you like, for it is not all one color. Then we brought water and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his hands and wiped his face, arms and head with the wetness of his hands three times. Then he said: O Akrash, this is ablution for what fire has changed. Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full, and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange and we do not know it except from his hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad and Affan told us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Shaiban told us. They said: Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us. Thabit told us. He said: Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by dreams. Sometimes a man saw a dream and asked about him if he did not know him. If someone praised him, he was more amazed by the dream. A woman came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I saw as if I came and was taken out of Madinah and entered Paradise. I heard a voice wailing for Paradise. I looked and saw so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so. I named twelve men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent out a detachment before that, and they were brought wearing satin garments with their jugular veins gushing. It was said: Take them to the river al-Baydakh or al-Baydakh. He said: So they dipped them in it and came out with their faces like the moon on a full moon night. Then a golden plate was brought on which were dates, and they ate as much of its dates as they wanted. They did not turn it one way or the other except that they ate as much of the fruit as they wanted. I ate with them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. The bearer of good tidings from that secret company said: “What happened was such and such a vision, and so-and-so and so-and-so were afflicted until he counted twelve men. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the woman and said: ‘Tell me your vision.’ So she told it and she kept saying: So-and-so and so-and-so were brought as he had said.” This is the wording of Abu Ya’la. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ said: This is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another will take its place. And the words of God, the Most High: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman al-Dab’i told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing in the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are soft birds. He said: One who eats them is softer than them. He said this three times. And I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. Ahmad alone transmitted it from this source. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Sifat Al-Jannah from the hadith of Ismail bin Ali Al-Khatmi from Ahmad bin Ali Al-Hayuti from Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim from Abdullah bin Ziyad from Zur’ah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar who said: Tuba was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Bakr, have you heard what Tuba is? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and none knows its height except God, like a camel. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, are there soft birds there? He said: Softer than that for those who eat it, and you are one of them, God willing. Qatada said regarding the verse: And the meat of birds of such as they desire, and he mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I see its birds soft as its people are soft. He said: “Who will eat it? By God, O Abu Bakr, it is softer than that, and it is like a camel. I hope to God that you will eat from it, O Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, Ma’n ibn Isa told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: “It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks, meaning like the necks of carrots.” Umar said: It is soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its food is softer than it. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, and he said: It is good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin al-Walid al-Rusafi, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a bird with seventy thousand feathers. It lands on the plate of a man from the people of Paradise, and he shakes it off. From each feather comes forth something whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. None of them resembles its owner in color. Then it flies away.” This is a very strange hadith, and al-Rusafi and his sheikh are weak. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, al-Layth told me, Khalid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka`b, who said: The birds of Paradise are like camels. They eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something from them, it comes until it lands in front of him, and eats from outside and inside, then it flies away without losing anything from it. It is authentic up to Ka`b. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. God the Almighty says: And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls. Some of them read it in the nominative case, meaning: And for them therein are fair maidens! The reading in the genitive case has two possible meanings: One of them is that the i’rab is in accordance with what precedes it, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Immortal youths will circulate among them * With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring * They will not suffer from headaches from it nor will they be exhausted * And fruit of whatever they choose * And the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire * And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes.” As God the Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet and as He the Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. The second possibility is that among what the immortal youths will circulate among them are the fair maidens, but that will be in palaces, not among one another, rather in tents, servants will circulate among them with the fair maidens, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Like hidden pearls means that they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and purity, as mentioned previously in Surat As-Saffat. Like hidden eggs was also described in Surat Ar-Rahman. That is why He said: A reward for what they used to do meaning that this is what We bestowed upon them as a reward for the good deeds they did. Then the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, they will hear no idle talk in Paradise, that is, vain talk devoid of meaning or containing a vile or weak meaning, as He said: Therein they will hear no idle talk, that is, a word of idle talk, nor sinful talk, that is, no speech that contains ugliness, “but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, except for the greeting of some of them to others, as the Almighty said: “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” And their speech is also free from idle talk and sinful talk.
56:14: God Almighty says, informing us about these forerunners who are brought near, that they are a group, that is, a group of the first ones and a few of the last ones. They differed about what is meant by His saying the first ones and the last ones. It was said that what is meant by the first ones are the past nations and by the last ones is this nation. This is a narration from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, narrated from them by Ibn Abi Hatim. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and he took as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the last ones who will be forerunners on the Day of Resurrection. He did not narrate anything else or attribute it to anyone. What is taken as evidence for this saying is what Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Muhammad Ibn Isa Ibn Al-Tabba’ told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the verse A group of the first ones * A few of the last ones was revealed, this was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise or…” Half of the people of Paradise and you will share the other half. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aswad bin Amir on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Muhammad the seller of silk on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it. A hadith similar to this was narrated from Jabir, and it was narrated by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir on the authority of Hisham bin Amara, who said: Abd Rabbih bin Salih told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the verse When the Event occurs was revealed, it mentioned a group of the former peoples and a few of the latter peoples. Umar said: O Messenger of God, a group of the former peoples and a few of us? He said: So he held off for a year at the end of the surah, then the verse, A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Umar, come and listen to what God has revealed: ‘A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones.’ Beware, from Adam to me there is a group, and my nation is a group, and we will not complete our third until we seek help from the black camel herders who testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.” This is how he included it in the biography of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, in both chain of transmission and text, but its chain of transmission is questionable. Many different chains of transmission have been narrated with the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, the hadith in full, and it is alone in describing Paradise, praise and thanks be to God. What Ibn Jarir chose here is questionable, rather it is a weak statement, because this nation is the best of nations according to the text of the Qur’an. It is unlikely that those who are brought near among others would be more than it, unless the sum of the nations is compared to this nation. It appears that those who are brought near among these people are more than all other nations, and God knows best. The second statement in this regard is the most correct, which is that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: A group of the former peoples means from the beginning of this nation, and a few of the latter peoples means from this nation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan told us, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Muzani told us, I heard Al-Hasan come to this verse, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” He said: As for the foremost, they have passed away, but O God, make us among the people of the right hand. Then he said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told us, he said: al-Hasan recited, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight. A company from the former peoples.” He said, A company from those who have passed away from this nation. My father told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said about this verse, “A company from the former peoples. And a few from the later peoples.” He said: They used to say, or hope, that they were all from this nation. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they were all from this nation. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than the last of it. So it is possible that the verse includes all nations, each nation according to its own circumstances. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahihs and other books from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The best of generations is my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. The hadith in full. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman told us, Ziyad Abu Umar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of my nation is like rain; it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better. This hadith, after determining the authenticity of its chain of transmission, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion is in need of the first of the nation to convey it to those who come after them, it is also in need of those who establish it at the end of it and to establish people upon the Sunnah, narrate it and make it known. The advantage is for the one who comes first. Likewise, the crops are in need of the first rain and the second rain, but the greater foundation is on the first and the crops’ need for it is more pressing, for were it not for it, it would not grow in the earth nor would its foundation be attached to it. For this reason, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. In another version: Until the command of God Almighty comes and they are like that. The point is that this nation is more noble than all other nations, and those who are close to God are more numerous than others and of a higher status due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason, it has been proven by continuous transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said, In this nation there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable. In another version, he said, With every thousand there will be seventy thousand. In another version, he said, With every one there will be seventy thousand. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham bin Yazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam - meaning Ibn Zur’ah - told me, on the authority of Shuraih - meaning Ibn Ubayd - on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a group like a black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say, ‘When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, more came than what came with the prophets, peace be upon them.’” It is good to mention here, when God Almighty says: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones, the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah, where he said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, Abu Amr bin Matar told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Mustafad al-Faryabi told us, Abu Wahb al-Walid bin Abdul Malik bin Ubayd God bin Masrah al-Harrani told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ al-Qurashi al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Zamil. Al-Juhani, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he would say while standing on his two feet, “Glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance,” seventy times. Then he would say, “Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in one day exceed seven hundred.” Then he would say that twice, then face the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be amazed by the vision and then say, Has any of you seen anything? Abu Zamil said: I said, O Messenger of God! He said, “Good you will encounter and evil you will avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Tell me your dream.” I said, “I saw all the people on a wide, easy, pleasant road, and the people were walking on the main road. While they were like that, the road passed by a meadow the likes of which my eyes had never seen before. It was flowing and its water dripped with various types of grass. He said, “It is as if I see the first group of people, when they reached the meadow, saying, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, not turning to the right or to the left.” He said, “It is as if I see them walking on. Then the second group came, and they were many times more numerous than them. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, some of them grazing and some of them taking small handfuls of food. They continued on like that.” He said, “Then the majority of the people came forward. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ and they said, ‘This is the best home.’ It is as if I see them turning to the right and to the left. When I saw that, I stuck to the road until I came to…” The furthest part of the meadow, and behold, O Messenger of God, I see you on a pulpit with seven steps, and you are on the highest step. And behold, to your right is a dark-skinned man with a hooked nose. When he speaks, he soars high that he surpasses the men in height. And behold, to your left is a man with a medium build, a large hawk, with a very handsome face, as if his hair had been bathed in water. When he speaks, you listen in respect of him. And behold, in front of him is an old man who most resembles you in appearance and face. All of you turn to him, seeking him. And behold, in front of him is a lean, lean she-camel. And behold, O Messenger of God, it is as if you are sending her forth. He said: The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned pale for a moment, then he was relieved, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for what you saw of the easy, spacious, and pleasant path, that is what I have carried you upon of guidance and you are upon it. As for the meadow that you saw, it is the world and the treachery of its life. I and my companions proceeded without clinging to anything from it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not return to it, and it did not return to us. Then the second group came after us, and they were many times more than us. Some of them graze and some take the handful, and they were saved on that. Then the majority of the people came and turned in the meadow to the right and to the left. So we belong to God, and to Him we shall return. As for you, you proceeded on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be on it until you meet me. As for the pulpit on which you saw seven steps, and I was at the highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am at the last of them for a thousand. As for the man whom you saw on my right, the thin-skinned one, that is Moses, peace be upon him. When he spoke, he rose above the men by virtue of God’s speech to him. And the one I saw on my left was the four-headed falcon, with many horses, as if his hair had been bathed in water. That is Jesus, son of Mary. We honor him because God honored him. As for the old man whom you saw most similar to me in appearance and face, that is our father Abraham. We all follow his example and imitate him. As for the she-camel that you saw and that you saw me sending, it is the Hour that will come upon us. There will be no prophet after me and no nation after my nation. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not asked about a vision after this except that a man would come and tell him about it voluntarily. God the Almighty said: “On couches adorned with gold.” Ibn Abbas said: meaning woven with gold, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Zaid bin Aslam, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. As-Suddi said: adorned with gold and pearls. Ikrimah said: adorned with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this the camel’s belly is called wadin, which is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul because it is braided. Likewise, the couches in Paradise are braided with gold and pearls. God the Almighty says: {Reclining on them, facing each other} meaning, their faces to each other, with no one behind the other. {Immortal youths will circulate around them} meaning, immortal in one condition, they will not be arrogant about it, they will not grow old, and they will not change. {With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring}. The goblets are the cups that have no spouts or ears, and the pitchers are the ones that combine the two descriptions, and the goblets are the ones that are drunk, and all of them are from wine from a flowing spring, not from vessels that stop and empty, but from gushing springs. God the Almighty says: {They will not suffer from headaches therefrom, nor will they lose their minds, rather they will be stable despite the intense, intoxicating pleasure and achieved pleasure. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There are four characteristics of wine: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urine. So God the Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and exonerated it from these characteristics. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Atiyah, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said, They do not suffer from headaches because of it, meaning they do not have a headache because of it. They said about His statement, nor are they intoxicated, meaning they do not lose their minds. And the Almighty said: And fruits of whatever they choose, and the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire. That is, they will be given whatever fruits they choose. This verse is evidence of the permissibility of eating fruits as they choose. This is indicated by the hadith of ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, which was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad. Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid Al-Tarsi told us, Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl ibn Abd Al-Malik ibn Abi Suwayyah told us, Ubayd God ibn ‘Ukrash told us, on the authority of his father, ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, who said: He once sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the alms tax on their wealth. I arrived in Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajireen and Ansar, and camels came to him that were like the roots of the Arta tree. He said, Who is this man? I said: Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb. He said: Raise your lineage. So I traced my lineage back to Murrah ibn Ubayd, and this is the charity of Murrah ibn Ubayd. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled and said: These are the camels of my people, these are the charity camels of my people. Then he ordered them to be branded with the brand of the charity camels and gathered with them. Then he took my hand and we set off to the house of Umm Salamah. He said: Is there any food? We were brought a large bowl-like dish full of tharid and flour, and he started eating from it. I started to beat its sides with my hand, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grabbed my right hand with his left hand and said: O Ukrash, eat from one place, for it is one food. Then a plate was brought to us containing dates or fresh dates. Ubaydullah was uncertain whether it was fresh dates or dried dates. I started to eat from what was in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) moved around in the plate and he said: O Ukrash, eat from wherever you like, for it is not all one color. Then we brought water and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his hands and wiped his face, arms and head with the wetness of his hands three times. Then he said: O Akrash, this is ablution for what fire has changed. Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full, and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange and we do not know it except from his hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad and Affan told us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Shaiban told us. They said: Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us. Thabit told us. He said: Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by dreams. Sometimes a man saw a dream and asked about him if he did not know him. If someone praised him, he was more amazed by the dream. A woman came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I saw as if I came and was taken out of Madinah and entered Paradise. I heard a voice wailing for Paradise. I looked and saw so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so. I named twelve men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent out a detachment before that, and they were brought wearing satin garments with their jugular veins gushing. It was said: Take them to the river al-Baydakh or al-Baydakh. He said: So they dipped them in it and came out with their faces like the moon on a full moon night. Then a golden plate was brought on which were dates, and they ate as much of its dates as they wanted. They did not turn it one way or the other except that they ate as much of the fruit as they wanted. I ate with them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. The bearer of good tidings from that secret company said: “What happened was such and such a vision, and so-and-so and so-and-so were afflicted until he counted twelve men. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the woman and said: ‘Tell me your vision.’ So she told it and she kept saying: So-and-so and so-and-so were brought as he had said.” This is the wording of Abu Ya’la. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ said: This is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another will take its place. And the words of God, the Most High: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman al-Dab’i told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing in the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are soft birds. He said: One who eats them is softer than them. He said this three times. And I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. Ahmad alone transmitted it from this source. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Sifat Al-Jannah from the hadith of Ismail bin Ali Al-Khatmi from Ahmad bin Ali Al-Hayuti from Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim from Abdullah bin Ziyad from Zur’ah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar who said: Tuba was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Bakr, have you heard what Tuba is? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and none knows its height except God, like a camel. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, are there soft birds there? He said: Softer than that for those who eat it, and you are one of them, God willing. Qatada said regarding the verse: And the meat of birds of such as they desire, and he mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I see its birds soft as its people are soft. He said: “Who will eat it? By God, O Abu Bakr, it is softer than that, and it is like a camel. I hope to God that you will eat from it, O Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, Ma’n ibn Isa told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: “It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks, meaning like the necks of carrots.” Umar said: It is soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its food is softer than it. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, and he said: It is good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin al-Walid al-Rusafi, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a bird with seventy thousand feathers. It lands on the plate of a man from the people of Paradise, and he shakes it off. From each feather comes forth something whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. None of them resembles its owner in color. Then it flies away.” This is a very strange hadith, and al-Rusafi and his sheikh are weak. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, al-Layth told me, Khalid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka`b, who said: The birds of Paradise are like camels. They eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something from them, it comes until it lands in front of him, and eats from outside and inside, then it flies away without losing anything from it. It is authentic up to Ka`b. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. God the Almighty says: And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls. Some of them read it in the nominative case, meaning: And for them therein are fair maidens! The reading in the genitive case has two possible meanings: One of them is that the i’rab is in accordance with what precedes it, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Immortal youths will circulate among them * With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring * They will not suffer from headaches from it nor will they be exhausted * And fruit of whatever they choose * And the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire * And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes.” As God the Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet and as He the Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. The second possibility is that among what the immortal youths will circulate among them are the fair maidens, but that will be in palaces, not among one another, rather in tents, servants will circulate among them with the fair maidens, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Like hidden pearls means that they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and purity, as mentioned previously in Surat As-Saffat. Like hidden eggs was also described in Surat Ar-Rahman. That is why He said: A reward for what they used to do meaning that this is what We bestowed upon them as a reward for the good deeds they did. Then the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, they will hear no idle talk in Paradise, that is, vain talk devoid of meaning or containing a vile or weak meaning, as He said: Therein they will hear no idle talk, that is, a word of idle talk, nor sinful talk, that is, no speech that contains ugliness, “but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, except for the greeting of some of them to others, as the Almighty said: “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” And their speech is also free from idle talk and sinful talk.
56:15: God Almighty says, informing us about these forerunners who are brought near, that they are a group, that is, a group of the first ones and a few of the last ones. They differed about what is meant by His saying the first ones and the last ones. It was said that what is meant by the first ones are the past nations and by the last ones is this nation. This is a narration from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, narrated from them by Ibn Abi Hatim. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and he took as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the last ones who will be forerunners on the Day of Resurrection. He did not narrate anything else or attribute it to anyone. What is taken as evidence for this saying is what Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Muhammad Ibn Isa Ibn Al-Tabba’ told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the verse A group of the first ones * A few of the last ones was revealed, this was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise or…” Half of the people of Paradise and you will share the other half. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aswad bin Amir on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Muhammad the seller of silk on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it. A hadith similar to this was narrated from Jabir, and it was narrated by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir on the authority of Hisham bin Amara, who said: Abd Rabbih bin Salih told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the verse When the Event occurs was revealed, it mentioned a group of the former peoples and a few of the latter peoples. Umar said: O Messenger of God, a group of the former peoples and a few of us? He said: So he held off for a year at the end of the surah, then the verse, A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Umar, come and listen to what God has revealed: ‘A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones.’ Beware, from Adam to me there is a group, and my nation is a group, and we will not complete our third until we seek help from the black camel herders who testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.” This is how he included it in the biography of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, in both chain of transmission and text, but its chain of transmission is questionable. Many different chains of transmission have been narrated with the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, the hadith in full, and it is alone in describing Paradise, praise and thanks be to God. What Ibn Jarir chose here is questionable, rather it is a weak statement, because this nation is the best of nations according to the text of the Qur’an. It is unlikely that those who are brought near among others would be more than it, unless the sum of the nations is compared to this nation. It appears that those who are brought near among these people are more than all other nations, and God knows best. The second statement in this regard is the most correct, which is that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: A group of the former peoples means from the beginning of this nation, and a few of the latter peoples means from this nation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan told us, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Muzani told us, I heard Al-Hasan come to this verse, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” He said: As for the foremost, they have passed away, but O God, make us among the people of the right hand. Then he said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told us, he said: al-Hasan recited, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight. A company from the former peoples.” He said, A company from those who have passed away from this nation. My father told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said about this verse, “A company from the former peoples. And a few from the later peoples.” He said: They used to say, or hope, that they were all from this nation. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they were all from this nation. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than the last of it. So it is possible that the verse includes all nations, each nation according to its own circumstances. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahihs and other books from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The best of generations is my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. The hadith in full. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman told us, Ziyad Abu Umar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of my nation is like rain; it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better. This hadith, after determining the authenticity of its chain of transmission, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion is in need of the first of the nation to convey it to those who come after them, it is also in need of those who establish it at the end of it and to establish people upon the Sunnah, narrate it and make it known. The advantage is for the one who comes first. Likewise, the crops are in need of the first rain and the second rain, but the greater foundation is on the first and the crops’ need for it is more pressing, for were it not for it, it would not grow in the earth nor would its foundation be attached to it. For this reason, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. In another version: Until the command of God Almighty comes and they are like that. The point is that this nation is more noble than all other nations, and those who are close to God are more numerous than others and of a higher status due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason, it has been proven by continuous transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said, In this nation there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable. In another version, he said, With every thousand there will be seventy thousand. In another version, he said, With every one there will be seventy thousand. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham bin Yazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam - meaning Ibn Zur’ah - told me, on the authority of Shuraih - meaning Ibn Ubayd - on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a group like a black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say, ‘When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, more came than what came with the prophets, peace be upon them.’” It is good to mention here, when God Almighty says: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones, the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah, where he said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, Abu Amr bin Matar told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Mustafad al-Faryabi told us, Abu Wahb al-Walid bin Abdul Malik bin Ubayd God bin Masrah al-Harrani told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ al-Qurashi al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Zamil. Al-Juhani, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he would say while standing on his two feet, “Glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance,” seventy times. Then he would say, “Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in one day exceed seven hundred.” Then he would say that twice, then face the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be amazed by the vision and then say, Has any of you seen anything? Abu Zamil said: I said, O Messenger of God! He said, “Good you will encounter and evil you will avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Tell me your dream.” I said, “I saw all the people on a wide, easy, pleasant road, and the people were walking on the main road.
