Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full, and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange and we do not know it except from his hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad and Affan told us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Shaiban told us. They said: Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us. Thabit told us. He said: Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by dreams. Sometimes a man saw a dream and asked about him if he did not know him. If someone praised him, he was more amazed by the dream. A woman came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I saw as if I came and was taken out of Madinah and entered Paradise. I heard a voice wailing for Paradise. I looked and saw so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so. I named twelve men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent out a detachment before that, and they were brought wearing satin garments with their jugular veins gushing. It was said: Take them to the river al-Baydakh or al-Baydakh. He said: So they dipped them in it and came out with their faces like the moon on a full moon night. Then a golden plate was brought on which were dates, and they ate as much of its dates as they wanted. They did not turn it one way or the other except that they ate as much of the fruit as they wanted. I ate with them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. The bearer of good tidings from that secret company said: “What happened was such and such a vision, and so-and-so and so-and-so were afflicted until he counted twelve men. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the woman and said: ‘Tell me your vision.’ So she told it and she kept saying: So-and-so and so-and-so were brought as he had said.” This is the wording of Abu Ya’la. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ said: This is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another will take its place. And the words of God, the Most High: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman al-Dab’i told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing in the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are soft birds. He said: One who eats them is softer than them. He said this three times. And I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. Ahmad alone transmitted it from this source. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Sifat Al-Jannah from the hadith of Ismail bin Ali Al-Khatmi from Ahmad bin Ali Al-Hayuti from Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim from Abdullah bin Ziyad from Zur’ah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar who said: Tuba was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Bakr, have you heard what Tuba is? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and none knows its height except God, like a camel. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, are there soft birds there? He said: Softer than that for those who eat it, and you are one of them, God willing. Qatada said regarding the verse: And the meat of birds of such as they desire, and he mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I see its birds soft as its people are soft. He said: “Who will eat it? By God, O Abu Bakr, it is softer than that, and it is like a camel. I hope to God that you will eat from it, O Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, Ma’n ibn Isa told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: “It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks, meaning like the necks of carrots.” Umar said: It is soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its food is softer than it. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, and he said: It is good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin al-Walid al-Rusafi, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a bird with seventy thousand feathers. It lands on the plate of a man from the people of Paradise, and he shakes it off. From each feather comes forth something whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. None of them resembles its owner in color. Then it flies away.” This is a very strange hadith, and al-Rusafi and his sheikh are weak. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, al-Layth told me, Khalid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka`b, who said: The birds of Paradise are like camels. They eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something from them, it comes until it lands in front of him, and eats from outside and inside, then it flies away without losing anything from it. It is authentic up to Ka`b. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. God the Almighty says: And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls. Some of them read it in the nominative case, meaning: And for them therein are fair maidens! The reading in the genitive case has two possible meanings: One of them is that the i’rab is in accordance with what precedes it, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Immortal youths will circulate among them * With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring * They will not suffer from headaches from it nor will they be exhausted * And fruit of whatever they choose * And the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire * And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes.” As God the Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet and as He the Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. The second possibility is that among what the immortal youths will circulate among them are the fair maidens, but that will be in palaces, not among one another, rather in tents, servants will circulate among them with the fair maidens, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Like hidden pearls means that they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and purity, as mentioned previously in Surat As-Saffat. Like hidden eggs was also described in Surat Ar-Rahman. That is why He said: A reward for what they used to do meaning that this is what We bestowed upon them as a reward for the good deeds they did. Then the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, they will hear no idle talk in Paradise, that is, vain talk devoid of meaning or containing a vile or weak meaning, as He said: Therein they will hear no idle talk, that is, a word of idle talk, nor sinful talk, that is, no speech that contains ugliness, “but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, except for the greeting of some of them to others, as the Almighty said: “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” And their speech is also free from idle talk and sinful talk.
56:25: God Almighty says, informing us about these forerunners who are brought near, that they are a group, that is, a group of the first ones and a few of the last ones. They differed about what is meant by His saying the first ones and the last ones. It was said that what is meant by the first ones are the past nations and by the last ones is this nation. This is a narration from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, narrated from them by Ibn Abi Hatim. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and he took as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the last ones who will be forerunners on the Day of Resurrection. He did not narrate anything else or attribute it to anyone. What is taken as evidence for this saying is what Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Muhammad Ibn Isa Ibn Al-Tabba’ told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the verse A group of the first ones * A few of the last ones was revealed, this was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise or…” Half of the people of Paradise and you will share the other half. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aswad bin Amir on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Muhammad the seller of silk on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it. A hadith similar to this was narrated from Jabir, and it was narrated by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir on the authority of Hisham bin Amara, who said: Abd Rabbih bin Salih told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the verse When the Event occurs was revealed, it mentioned a group of the former peoples and a few of the latter peoples. Umar said: O Messenger of God, a group of the former peoples and a few of us? He said: So he held off for a year at the end of the surah, then the verse, A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Umar, come and listen to what God has revealed: ‘A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones.’ Beware, from Adam to me there is a group, and my nation is a group, and we will not complete our third until we seek help from the black camel herders who testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.” This is how he included it in the biography of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, in both chain of transmission and text, but its chain of transmission is questionable. Many different chains of transmission have been narrated with the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, the hadith in full, and it is alone in describing Paradise, praise and thanks be to God. What Ibn Jarir chose here is questionable, rather it is a weak statement, because this nation is the best of nations according to the text of the Qur’an. It is unlikely that those who are brought near among others would be more than it, unless the sum of the nations is compared to this nation. It appears that those who are brought near among these people are more than all other nations, and God knows best. The second statement in this regard is the most correct, which is that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: A group of the former peoples means from the beginning of this nation, and a few of the latter peoples means from this nation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan told us, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Muzani told us, I heard Al-Hasan come to this verse, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” He said: As for the foremost, they have passed away, but O God, make us among the people of the right hand. Then he said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told us, he said: al-Hasan recited, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight. A company from the former peoples.” He said, A company from those who have passed away from this nation. My father told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said about this verse, “A company from the former peoples. And a few from the later peoples.” He said: They used to say, or hope, that they were all from this nation. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they were all from this nation. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than the last of it. So it is possible that the verse includes all nations, each nation according to its own circumstances. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahihs and other books from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The best of generations is my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. The hadith in full. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman told us, Ziyad Abu Umar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of my nation is like rain; it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better. This hadith, after determining the authenticity of its chain of transmission, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion is in need of the first of the nation to convey it to those who come after them, it is also in need of those who establish it at the end of it and to establish people upon the Sunnah, narrate it and make it known. The advantage is for the one who comes first. Likewise, the crops are in need of the first rain and the second rain, but the greater foundation is on the first and the crops’ need for it is more pressing, for were it not for it, it would not grow in the earth nor would its foundation be attached to it. For this reason, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. In another version: Until the command of God Almighty comes and they are like that. The point is that this nation is more noble than all other nations, and those who are close to God are more numerous than others and of a higher status due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason, it has been proven by continuous transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said, In this nation there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable. In another version, he said, With every thousand there will be seventy thousand. In another version, he said, With every one there will be seventy thousand. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham bin Yazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam - meaning Ibn Zur’ah - told me, on the authority of Shuraih - meaning Ibn Ubayd - on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a group like a black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say, ‘When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, more came than what came with the prophets, peace be upon them.’” It is good to mention here, when God Almighty says: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones, the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah, where he said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, Abu Amr bin Matar told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Mustafad al-Faryabi told us, Abu Wahb al-Walid bin Abdul Malik bin Ubayd God bin Masrah al-Harrani told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ al-Qurashi al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Zamil. Al-Juhani, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he would say while standing on his two feet, “Glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance,” seventy times. Then he would say, “Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in one day exceed seven hundred.” Then he would say that twice, then face the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be amazed by the vision and then say, Has any of you seen anything? Abu Zamil said: I said, O Messenger of God! He said, “Good you will encounter and evil you will avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Tell me your dream.” I said, “I saw all the people on a wide, easy, pleasant road, and the people were walking on the main road. While they were like that, the road passed by a meadow the likes of which my eyes had never seen before. It was flowing and its water dripped with various types of grass. He said, “It is as if I see the first group of people, when they reached the meadow, saying, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, not turning to the right or to the left.” He said, “It is as if I see them walking on. Then the second group came, and they were many times more numerous than them. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, some of them grazing and some of them taking small handfuls of food. They continued on like that.” He said, “Then the majority of the people came forward. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ and they said, ‘This is the best home.’ It is as if I see them turning to the right and to the left. When I saw that, I stuck to the road until I came to…” The furthest part of the meadow, and behold, O Messenger of God, I see you on a pulpit with seven steps, and you are on the highest step. And behold, to your right is a dark-skinned man with a hooked nose. When he speaks, he soars high that he surpasses the men in height. And behold, to your left is a man with a medium build, a large hawk, with a very handsome face, as if his hair had been bathed in water. When he speaks, you listen in respect of him. And behold, in front of him is an old man who most resembles you in appearance and face. All of you turn to him, seeking him. And behold, in front of him is a lean, lean she-camel. And behold, O Messenger of God, it is as if you are sending her forth. He said: The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned pale for a moment, then he was relieved, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for what you saw of the easy, spacious, and pleasant path, that is what I have carried you upon of guidance and you are upon it. As for the meadow that you saw, it is the world and the treachery of its life. I and my companions proceeded without clinging to anything from it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not return to it, and it did not return to us. Then the second group came after us, and they were many times more than us. Some of them graze and some take the handful, and they were saved on that. Then the majority of the people came and turned in the meadow to the right and to the left. So we belong to God, and to Him we shall return. As for you, you proceeded on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be on it until you meet me. As for the pulpit on which you saw seven steps, and I was at the highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am at the last of them for a thousand. As for the man whom you saw on my right, the thin-skinned one, that is Moses, peace be upon him. When he spoke, he rose above the men by virtue of God’s speech to him. And the one I saw on my left was the four-headed falcon, with many horses, as if his hair had been bathed in water. That is Jesus, son of Mary. We honor him because God honored him. As for the old man whom you saw most similar to me in appearance and face, that is our father Abraham. We all follow his example and imitate him. As for the she-camel that you saw and that you saw me sending, it is the Hour that will come upon us. There will be no prophet after me and no nation after my nation. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not asked about a vision after this except that a man would come and tell him about it voluntarily. God the Almighty said: “On couches adorned with gold.” Ibn Abbas said: meaning woven with gold, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Zaid bin Aslam, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. As-Suddi said: adorned with gold and pearls. Ikrimah said: adorned with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this the camel’s belly is called wadin, which is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul because it is braided. Likewise, the couches in Paradise are braided with gold and pearls. God the Almighty says: {Reclining on them, facing each other} meaning, their faces to each other, with no one behind the other. {Immortal youths will circulate around them} meaning, immortal in one condition, they will not be arrogant about it, they will not grow old, and they will not change. {With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring}. The goblets are the cups that have no spouts or ears, and the pitchers are the ones that combine the two descriptions, and the goblets are the ones that are drunk, and all of them are from wine from a flowing spring, not from vessels that stop and empty, but from gushing springs. God the Almighty says: {They will not suffer from headaches therefrom, nor will they lose their minds, rather they will be stable despite the intense, intoxicating pleasure and achieved pleasure. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There are four characteristics of wine: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urine. So God the Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and exonerated it from these characteristics. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Atiyah, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said, They do not suffer from headaches because of it, meaning they do not have a headache because of it. They said about His statement, nor are they intoxicated, meaning they do not lose their minds. And the Almighty said: And fruits of whatever they choose, and the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire. That is, they will be given whatever fruits they choose. This verse is evidence of the permissibility of eating fruits as they choose. This is indicated by the hadith of ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, which was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad. Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid Al-Tarsi told us, Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl ibn Abd Al-Malik ibn Abi Suwayyah told us, Ubayd God ibn ‘Ukrash told us, on the authority of his father, ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, who said: He once sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the alms tax on their wealth. I arrived in Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajireen and Ansar, and camels came to him that were like the roots of the Arta tree. He said, Who is this man? I said: Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb. He said: Raise your lineage. So I traced my lineage back to Murrah ibn Ubayd, and this is the charity of Murrah ibn Ubayd. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled and said: These are the camels of my people, these are the charity camels of my people. Then he ordered them to be branded with the brand of the charity camels and gathered with them. Then he took my hand and we set off to the house of Umm Salamah. He said: Is there any food? We were brought a large bowl-like dish full of tharid and flour, and he started eating from it. I started to beat its sides with my hand, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grabbed my right hand with his left hand and said: O Ukrash, eat from one place, for it is one food. Then a plate was brought to us containing dates or fresh dates. Ubaydullah was uncertain whether it was fresh dates or dried dates. I started to eat from what was in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) moved around in the plate and he said: O Ukrash, eat from wherever you like, for it is not all one color. Then we brought water and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his hands and wiped his face, arms and head with the wetness of his hands three times. Then he said: O Akrash, this is ablution for what fire has changed. Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full, and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange and we do not know it except from his hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad and Affan told us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Shaiban told us. They said: Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us. Thabit told us. He said: Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by dreams. Sometimes a man saw a dream and asked about him if he did not know him. If someone praised him, he was more amazed by the dream. A woman came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I saw as if I came and was taken out of Madinah and entered Paradise. I heard a voice wailing for Paradise. I looked and saw so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so. I named twelve men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent out a detachment before that, and they were brought wearing satin garments with their jugular veins gushing. It was said: Take them to the river al-Baydakh or al-Baydakh. He said: So they dipped them in it and came out with their faces like the moon on a full moon night. Then a golden plate was brought on which were dates, and they ate as much of its dates as they wanted. They did not turn it one way or the other except that they ate as much of the fruit as they wanted. I ate with them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. The bearer of good tidings from that secret company said: “What happened was such and such a vision, and so-and-so and so-and-so were afflicted until he counted twelve men. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the woman and said: ‘Tell me your vision.’ So she told it and she kept saying: So-and-so and so-and-so were brought as he had said.” This is the wording of Abu Ya’la. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ said: This is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another will take its place. And the words of God, the Most High: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman al-Dab’i told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing in the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are soft birds. He said: One who eats them is softer than them. He said this three times. And I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. Ahmad alone transmitted it from this source. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Sifat Al-Jannah from the hadith of Ismail bin Ali Al-Khatmi from Ahmad bin Ali Al-Hayuti from Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim from Abdullah bin Ziyad from Zur’ah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar who said: Tuba was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Bakr, have you heard what Tuba is? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and none knows its height except God, like a camel. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, are there soft birds there? He said: Softer than that for those who eat it, and you are one of them, God willing. Qatada said regarding the verse: And the meat of birds of such as they desire, and he mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I see its birds soft as its people are soft. He said: “Who will eat it? By God, O Abu Bakr, it is softer than that, and it is like a camel. I hope to God that you will eat from it, O Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, Ma’n ibn Isa told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: “It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks, meaning like the necks of carrots.” Umar said: It is soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its food is softer than it. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, and he said: It is good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin al-Walid al-Rusafi, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a bird with seventy thousand feathers. It lands on the plate of a man from the people of Paradise, and he shakes it off. From each feather comes forth something whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. None of them resembles its owner in color. Then it flies away.” This is a very strange hadith, and al-Rusafi and his sheikh are weak. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, al-Layth told me, Khalid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka`b, who said: The birds of Paradise are like camels. They eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something from them, it comes until it lands in front of him, and eats from outside and inside, then it flies away without losing anything from it. It is authentic up to Ka`b. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. God the Almighty says: And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls. Some of them read it in the nominative case, meaning: And for them therein are fair maidens! The reading in the genitive case has two possible meanings: One of them is that the i’rab is in accordance with what precedes it, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Immortal youths will circulate among them * With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring * They will not suffer from headaches from it nor will they be exhausted * And fruit of whatever they choose * And the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire * And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes.” As God the Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet and as He the Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. The second possibility is that among what the immortal youths will circulate among them are the fair maidens, but that will be in palaces, not among one another, rather in tents, servants will circulate among them with the fair maidens, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Like hidden pearls means that they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and purity, as mentioned previously in Surat As-Saffat. Like hidden eggs was also described in Surat Ar-Rahman. That is why He said: A reward for what they used to do meaning that this is what We bestowed upon them as a reward for the good deeds they did. Then the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, they will hear no idle talk in Paradise, that is, vain talk devoid of meaning or containing a vile or weak meaning, as He said: Therein they will hear no idle talk, that is, a word of idle talk, nor sinful talk, that is, no speech that contains ugliness, “but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, except for the greeting of some of them to others, as the Almighty said: “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” And their speech is also free from idle talk and sinful talk.
56:26: God Almighty says, informing us about these forerunners who are brought near, that they are a group, that is, a group of the first ones and a few of the last ones. They differed about what is meant by His saying the first ones and the last ones. It was said that what is meant by the first ones are the past nations and by the last ones is this nation. This is a narration from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, narrated from them by Ibn Abi Hatim. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and he took as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the last ones who will be forerunners on the Day of Resurrection. He did not narrate anything else or attribute it to anyone. What is taken as evidence for this saying is what Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Muhammad Ibn Isa Ibn Al-Tabba’ told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the verse A group of the first ones * A few of the last ones was revealed, this was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise or…” Half of the people of Paradise and you will share the other half. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aswad bin Amir on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Muhammad the seller of silk on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it. A hadith similar to this was narrated from Jabir, and it was narrated by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir on the authority of Hisham bin Amara, who said: Abd Rabbih bin Salih told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the verse When the Event occurs was revealed, it mentioned a group of the former peoples and a few of the latter peoples. Umar said: O Messenger of God, a group of the former peoples and a few of us? He said: So he held off for a year at the end of the surah, then the verse, A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Umar, come and listen to what God has revealed: ‘A group of the former peoples * And a group of the latter ones.’ Beware, from Adam to me there is a group, and my nation is a group, and we will not complete our third until we seek help from the black camel herders who testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.” This is how he included it in the biography of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, in both chain of transmission and text, but its chain of transmission is questionable. Many different chains of transmission have been narrated with the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, the hadith in full, and it is alone in describing Paradise, praise and thanks be to God. What Ibn Jarir chose here is questionable, rather it is a weak statement, because this nation is the best of nations according to the text of the Qur’an. It is unlikely that those who are brought near among others would be more than it, unless the sum of the nations is compared to this nation. It appears that those who are brought near among these people are more than all other nations, and God knows best. The second statement in this regard is the most correct, which is that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: A group of the former peoples means from the beginning of this nation, and a few of the latter peoples means from this nation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan told us, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Muzani told us, I heard Al-Hasan come to this verse, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” He said: As for the foremost, they have passed away, but O God, make us among the people of the right hand. Then he said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told us, he said: al-Hasan recited, “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the Gardens of Delight. A company from the former peoples.” He said, A company from those who have passed away from this nation. My father told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said about this verse, “A company from the former peoples. And a few from the later peoples.” He said: They used to say, or hope, that they were all from this nation. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they were all from this nation. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than the last of it. So it is possible that the verse includes all nations, each nation according to its own circumstances. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahihs and other books from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The best of generations is my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. The hadith in full. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman told us, Ziyad Abu Umar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of my nation is like rain; it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better. This hadith, after determining the authenticity of its chain of transmission, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion is in need of the first of the nation to convey it to those who come after them, it is also in need of those who establish it at the end of it and to establish people upon the Sunnah, narrate it and make it known. The advantage is for the one who comes first. Likewise, the crops are in need of the first rain and the second rain, but the greater foundation is on the first and the crops’ need for it is more pressing, for were it not for it, it would not grow in the earth nor would its foundation be attached to it. For this reason, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to prevail upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. In another version: Until the command of God Almighty comes and they are like that. The point is that this nation is more noble than all other nations, and those who are close to God are more numerous than others and of a higher status due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason, it has been proven by continuous transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said, In this nation there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable. In another version, he said, With every thousand there will be seventy thousand. In another version, he said, With every one there will be seventy thousand. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham bin Yazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam - meaning Ibn Zur’ah - told me, on the authority of Shuraih - meaning Ibn Ubayd - on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a group like a black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say, ‘When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, more came than what came with the prophets, peace be upon them.’” It is good to mention here, when God Almighty says: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones, the hadith that al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah, where he said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, Abu Amr bin Matar told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Mustafad al-Faryabi told us, Abu Wahb al-Walid bin Abdul Malik bin Ubayd God bin Masrah al-Harrani told us, Sulayman bin Ata’ al-Qurashi al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Zamil. Al-Juhani, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he would say while standing on his two feet, “Glory be to God and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance,” seventy times. Then he would say, “Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in one day exceed seven hundred.” Then he would say that twice, then face the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be amazed by the vision and then say, Has any of you seen anything? Abu Zamil said: I said, O Messenger of God! He said, “Good you will encounter and evil you will avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Tell me your dream.” I said, “I saw all the people on a wide, easy, pleasant road, and the people were walking on the main road. While they were like that, the road passed by a meadow the likes of which my eyes had never seen before. It was flowing and its water dripped with various types of grass. He said, “It is as if I see the first group of people, when they reached the meadow, saying, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, not turning to the right or to the left.” He said, “It is as if I see them walking on. Then the second group came, and they were many times more numerous than them. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then they leaned on their mounts in the road, some of them grazing and some of them taking small handfuls of food. They continued on like that.” He said, “Then the majority of the people came forward. When they reached the meadow, they said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ and they said, ‘This is the best home.’ It is as if I see them turning to the right and to the left. When I saw that, I stuck to the road until I came to…” The furthest part of the meadow, and behold, O Messenger of God, I see you on a pulpit with seven steps, and you are on the highest step. And behold, to your right is a dark-skinned man with a hooked nose. When he speaks, he soars high that he surpasses the men in height. And behold, to your left is a man with a medium build, a large hawk, with a very handsome face, as if his hair had been bathed in water. When he speaks, you listen in respect of him. And behold, in front of him is an old man who most resembles you in appearance and face. All of you turn to him, seeking him. And behold, in front of him is a lean, lean she-camel. And behold, O Messenger of God, it is as if you are sending her forth. He said: The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned pale for a moment, then he was relieved, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for what you saw of the easy, spacious, and pleasant path, that is what I have carried you upon of guidance and you are upon it. As for the meadow that you saw, it is the world and the treachery of its life. I and my companions proceeded without clinging to anything from it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not return to it, and it did not return to us. Then the second group came after us, and they were many times more than us. Some of them graze and some take the handful, and they were saved on that. Then the majority of the people came and turned in the meadow to the right and to the left. So we belong to God, and to Him we shall return. As for you, you proceeded on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be on it until you meet me. As for the pulpit on which you saw seven steps, and I was at the highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am at the last of them for a thousand. As for the man whom you saw on my right, the thin-skinned one, that is Moses, peace be upon him. When he spoke, he rose above the men by virtue of God’s speech to him. And the one I saw on my left was the four-headed falcon, with many horses, as if his hair had been bathed in water. That is Jesus, son of Mary. We honor him because God honored him. As for the old man whom you saw most similar to me in appearance and face, that is our father Abraham. We all follow his example and imitate him. As for the she-camel that you saw and that you saw me sending, it is the Hour that will come upon us. There will be no prophet after me and no nation after my nation. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not asked about a vision after this except that a man would come and tell him about it voluntarily. God the Almighty said: “On couches adorned with gold.” Ibn Abbas said: meaning woven with gold, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Zaid bin Aslam, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. As-Suddi said: adorned with gold and pearls. Ikrimah said: adorned with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this the camel’s belly is called wadin, which is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul because it is braided. Likewise, the couches in Paradise are braided with gold and pearls. God the Almighty says: {Reclining on them, facing each other} meaning, their faces to each other, with no one behind the other. {Immortal youths will circulate around them} meaning, immortal in one condition, they will not be arrogant about it, they will not grow old, and they will not change. {With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring}. The goblets are the cups that have no spouts or ears, and the pitchers are the ones that combine the two descriptions, and the goblets are the ones that are drunk, and all of them are from wine from a flowing spring, not from vessels that stop and empty, but from gushing springs. God the Almighty says: {They will not suffer from headaches therefrom, nor will they lose their minds, rather they will be stable despite the intense, intoxicating pleasure and achieved pleasure. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There are four characteristics of wine: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urine. So God the Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and exonerated it from these characteristics. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Atiyah, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said, They do not suffer from headaches because of it, meaning they do not have a headache because of it. They said about His statement, nor are they intoxicated, meaning they do not lose their minds. And the Almighty said: And fruits of whatever they choose, and the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire. That is, they will be given whatever fruits they choose. This verse is evidence of the permissibility of eating fruits as they choose. This is indicated by the hadith of ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, which was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad. Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid Al-Tarsi told us, Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl ibn Abd Al-Malik ibn Abi Suwayyah told us, Ubayd God ibn ‘Ukrash told us, on the authority of his father, ‘Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb, who said: He once sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the alms tax on their wealth. I arrived in Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajireen and Ansar, and camels came to him that were like the roots of the Arta tree. He said, Who is this man? I said: Ukrash ibn Dhu’ayb. He said: Raise your lineage. So I traced my lineage back to Murrah ibn Ubayd, and this is the charity of Murrah ibn Ubayd. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled and said: These are the camels of my people, these are the charity camels of my people. Then he ordered them to be branded with the brand of the charity camels and gathered with them. Then he took my hand and we set off to the house of Umm Salamah. He said: Is there any food? We were brought a large bowl-like dish full of tharid and flour, and he started eating from it. I started to beat its sides with my hand, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grabbed my right hand with his left hand and said: O Ukrash, eat from one place, for it is one food. Then a plate was brought to us containing dates or fresh dates. Ubaydullah was uncertain whether it was fresh dates or dried dates. I started to eat from what was in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) moved around in the plate and he said: O Ukrash, eat from wherever you like, for it is not all one color. Then we brought water and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his hands and wiped his face, arms and head with the wetness of his hands three times. Then he said: O Akrash, this is ablution for what fire has changed. Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in full, and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Fadl, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange and we do not know it except from his hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad and Affan told us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Shaiban told us. They said: Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us. Thabit told us. He said: Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by dreams. Sometimes a man saw a dream and asked about him if he did not know him. If someone praised him, he was more amazed by the dream. A woman came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I saw as if I came and was taken out of Madinah and entered Paradise. I heard a voice wailing for Paradise. I looked and saw so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so. I named twelve men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent out a detachment before that, and they were brought wearing satin garments with their jugular veins gushing. It was said: Take them to the river al-Baydakh or al-Baydakh. He said: So they dipped them in it and came out with their faces like the moon on a full moon night. Then a golden plate was brought on which were dates, and they ate as much of its dates as they wanted. They did not turn it one way or the other except that they ate as much of the fruit as they wanted. I ate with them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. The bearer of good tidings from that secret company said: “What happened was such and such a vision, and so-and-so and so-and-so were afflicted until he counted twelve men. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the woman and said: ‘Tell me your vision.’ So she told it and she kept saying: So-and-so and so-and-so were brought as he had said.” This is the wording of Abu Ya’la. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ said: This is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another will take its place. And the words of God, the Most High: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar ibn Hatim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman al-Dab’i told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing in the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are soft birds. He said: One who eats them is softer than them. He said this three times. And I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. Ahmad alone transmitted it from this source. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Sifat Al-Jannah from the hadith of Ismail bin Ali Al-Khatmi from Ahmad bin Ali Al-Hayuti from Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim from Abdullah bin Ziyad from Zur’ah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar who said: Tuba was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Bakr, have you heard what Tuba is? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and none knows its height except God, like a camel. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, are there soft birds there? He said: Softer than that for those who eat it, and you are one of them, God willing. Qatada said regarding the verse: And the meat of birds of such as they desire, and he mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I see its birds soft as its people are soft. He said: “Who will eat it? By God, O Abu Bakr, it is softer than that, and it is like a camel. I hope to God that you will eat from it, O Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, Ma’n ibn Isa told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: “It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks, meaning like the necks of carrots.” Umar said: It is soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its food is softer than it. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, and he said: It is good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin al-Walid al-Rusafi, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a bird with seventy thousand feathers. It lands on the plate of a man from the people of Paradise, and he shakes it off. From each feather comes forth something whiter than milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey. None of them resembles its owner in color. Then it flies away.” This is a very strange hadith, and al-Rusafi and his sheikh are weak. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, told us, al-Layth told me, Khalid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ka`b, who said: The birds of Paradise are like camels. They eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something from them, it comes until it lands in front of him, and eats from outside and inside, then it flies away without losing anything from it. It is authentic up to Ka`b. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. God the Almighty says: And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls. Some of them read it in the nominative case, meaning: And for them therein are fair maidens! The reading in the genitive case has two possible meanings: One of them is that the i’rab is in accordance with what precedes it, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Immortal youths will circulate among them * With goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring * They will not suffer from headaches from it nor will they be exhausted * And fruit of whatever they choose * And the flesh of fowl of whatever they desire * And fair maidens of large, beautiful eyes.” As God the Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet and as He the Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. The second possibility is that among what the immortal youths will circulate among them are the fair maidens, but that will be in palaces, not among one another, rather in tents, servants will circulate among them with the fair maidens, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Like hidden pearls means that they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and purity, as mentioned previously in Surat As-Saffat. Like hidden eggs was also described in Surat Ar-Rahman. That is why He said: A reward for what they used to do meaning that this is what We bestowed upon them as a reward for the good deeds they did. Then the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, they will hear no idle talk in Paradise, that is, vain talk devoid of meaning or containing a vile or weak meaning, as He said: Therein they will hear no idle talk, that is, a word of idle talk, nor sinful talk, that is, no speech that contains ugliness, “but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” That is, except for the greeting of some of them to others, as the Almighty said: “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” And their speech is also free from idle talk and sinful talk.
56:27: When God Almighty mentioned the fate of the forerunners, who are the close ones, He followed them by mentioning the companions of the right, who are the righteous, as Maymun ibn Mihran said, the status of the companions of the right is lower than the close ones, so He said, And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right? meaning, who are the companions of the right, what is their state, and what is their fate? Then he explained that, saying, In thornless lote trees. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibn Al-Ahwas, Qasama bin Zuhair, Al-Safar bin Qais, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah bin Kathir, Al-Suddi, Abu Hazra, and others said: It is the one that has no thorns. And from Ibn Abbas: It is the one that is laden with fruit. This is a narration from Ikrimah and Mujahid. And Qatadah also said: We used to say that it is the one that is laden with thorns. And it appears that what is meant is this and that. For the lote tree of this world has many thorns and little fruit, and in the Hereafter, on the contrary, it has no thorns and has many fruits that have weighed down its root, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Salman Al-Najjad said: Muhammad bin Muhammad, he is Al-Baghawi, told us. Hamza bin Abbas told me. Abdullah bin Uthman told us. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us. Safwan bin Amr told us, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions. He said: One day a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned in Paradise a tree that harms…” Its owner, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: What are they? He said: The lote tree, for it has harmful thorns. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘In a lote tree without thorns’? God trimmed its thorns and replaced each thorn with a fruit. It produces fruit, each of which reveals seventy-two types of food, and no color is similar to the other.” Another path Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud said: Muhammad bin Al-Musaffa told us, Muhammad bin Al-Mubarak told us, Yahya bin Hamza told me, Thawr bin Yazid told me, Habib bin Ubaid told me on the authority of Utbah bin Abdul Salami, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, I hear you mention a tree in Paradise, and I do not know of a tree with more thorns than it, meaning the talh tree. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God will place in place of every thorn in it a fruit like the testicle of a groomed goat, in which there are seventy types of food, no color resembling another. And his saying: And talh in layers, talh is a large tree that grows in the land of the Hijaz from the ‘adah tree, the singular of which is talha, and it is a tree with many thorns. Ibn Jarir recited to one of the hadith scholars: Her guide gave her good report and said, Tomorrow you will see the acacia trees and the mountains. Mujahed said: Mandhud means piled up with fruit. This reminds us of the Quraysh because they used to marvel at the shade of the Talh and Sidr trees. Al-Suddi said: Mandhud is masfud. Ibn Abbas said: It resembles the Talh of this world, but its fruit is sweeter than honey. Al-Jawhari said: Talh is a dialect for stalk. I said: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Al-Hasan bin Sa’d from a sheikh from Hamdan who said: I heard Ali say this word about Talh Mandhud. He said: A piled up stalk. Based on this, it is a description of the Sidr, so it is as if he described it as being makhdhud, which means that it has no thorns, and that its stalk is mandhud which means the abundance of its fruit. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Idris, on the authority of Jaafar bin Iyas, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, And Talh Mandhud, meaning bananas. He said: And it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qassama bin Zuhair, Qatadah, and Abu Hazra something similar, and with it. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: And he added and said: The people of Yemen call bananas Talh. Ibn Jarir did not narrate anything other than this statement. And the Almighty’s saying: And an extended shade. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, conveying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing the line. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it likewise from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. And thus Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan on the authority of Falih on his authority, and thus Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and thus Hammad bin Salamah narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Al-Layth bin Saad on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and Aouf on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Hajjaj told us: Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu Ad-Dahhak telling Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for seventy or one hundred years. It is the tree of eternity.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for one hundred years, but he would not be able to cross it. And if you wish, recite: ‘and an extended shade.’” The chain of transmission is good, but they did not include it. Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of `Abdah, `Abd al-Rahim, and al-Bukhari, all on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr, on his authority. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider can travel for a hundred years. Read if you wish: and an extended shade. When that reached Ka’b, he said: He has spoken the truth, by He who sent down the Torah to Moses and the Criterion to Muhammad. If a man were to ride on a tree trunk or a tree stump, then circle around the top of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down in old age. God planted it with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise except that it flows from the base of that tree. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Munhal al-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: and extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Al-Bukhari narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ruh ibn ‘Abd al-Mu’min, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Imran ibn Dawud al-Qattan, on the authority of Qatadah, and in the same way, Muammar and Abu Hilal narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Qatadah. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa’id and Sahl ibn Sa’d, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. This hadith is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and is mutawatir and its authenticity is confirmed by the leading critics of hadith, due to the multiplicity of its chains of transmission, the strength of its isnads, and the trustworthiness of its men. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Abu Hasin narrated to us: We were at a door in a place and with us were Abu Salih and Shuqaiq, meaning Ad-Dhabi. Abu Salih narrated: Abu Hurairah narrated to me: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider would travel for seventy years. Abu Salih said: Do you accuse Abu Hurairah of lying? He said: I do not accuse Abu Hurairah of lying, but I accuse you of lying. This was difficult for the reciters of hadith at that time. I said: Whoever accuses this hadith has invalidated it, even though it is proven and authentic and traced back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tirmidhi said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ziyad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Furat Al-Qazzaz narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no tree in Paradise but its trunk is made of gold. Then he said: Good and strange. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi narrated to us, on the authority of Zam’ah bin Salih, on the authority of Salamah bin Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The extended shade is a tree in Paradise, and its shade is as long as a rider can travel in all its directions, a hundred years. He said: The people of Paradise, the people of the upper rooms and others, will come out to it and converse in its shade. He said: Some of them will desire it and remember the amusement of this world, so God will send a wind from Paradise, and that tree will stir with every amusement in this world. This is a strange narration, its chain of transmission is good, strong, and good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashja’ narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, regarding the verse: and an extended shade, he said: seventy thousand years. Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, similarly. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, and an extended shade, he said: five hundred thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Husayn ibn Nafi’ told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Auf said, on the authority of al-Hasan: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Shabib said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In Paradise there are trees that cannot be carried to shelter oneself under them. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Hazra said regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, that is, it does not end, there is no sun or heat in it like before dawn. Ibn Mas’ud said: Paradise is covered with curtains like the time between dawn and sunrise. Verses have come before, such as the statement of God, the Most High: And We will admit them into a deep shade, and His statement: Its food is everlasting and its shade, and His statement: In shades and springs, and other verses. And His statement: God the Almighty said: And flowing water. Al-Thawri said: It flows without a trench. We have already discussed the interpretation of God the Almighty’s statement: Therein are rivers of water that is not stagnant, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And the Almighty said: And abundant fruit, neither forbidden nor forbidden. That is, they will have abundant fruits of various colors that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as the Almighty said: Whenever they are provided with fruit therefrom as provision, they say, ‘This is what we were provided with before.’ And they will be given it in resemblance. That is, the shape resembles the shape, but the taste is different. And in the two Sahihs, when mentioning the lote tree of the farthest boundary, it says: Then behold, its leaves are like the ears of elephants, and its dates are like the jars of Hajar. And in them also from the hadith of Malik from Zaid from Ata’ ibn Yasar from Ibn Abbas who said: The sun eclipsed and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed and the people were with him and he mentioned the prayer, and in it they said: O Messenger of God, we saw you reach for something in this place of yours and then we saw you slump down, he said: I saw Paradise and reached for a bunch of grapes from it, and if I had taken it you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained. And Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Abdullah ibn Ja’far told us, Ubaydullah told us, Ibn Aqil told us from Jabir who said: While we were praying the noon prayer, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward and we moved forward with him, then he reached for something to take it and then he stepped back, and when he had finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: O Messenger of God, today you did something in the prayer that you did not do, he said: “Paradise and what is in it of flowers and freshness were shown to me, and I reached for a bunch of grapes from it to bring it to you, but I was prevented from it, and if I brought it to you, I would eat from it from between the sky and the earth and it would not be diminished.” And Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Bahr told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about the Cistern. He mentioned Paradise, then the Bedouin said: Is there fruit in it? He said: Yes, and in it is a tree called Tuba. He said: Then he mentioned something, but I do not know what it was. He said: What tree of our land does it resemble? He said: It does not resemble any of the trees of your land? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you been to Syria? He said: No. He said: “It resembles a tree in Syria called al-Jawzah. It grows on one stem and its top is spread out.” He said: How big is the cluster? He said: A month’s journey for the speckled crow that does not stop. He said: How big is its root? He said: If a young camel from your family were to set out on a journey, it would not reach its root until its collarbone would break from old age. He said: In it are grapes? He said: Yes. He said: How big is the seed? He said, Did your father ever slaughter a large goat from his flock? He said, Yes. He said, He skinned its hide and gave it to your mother and said, 'Make us a bucket from it?' He said, Yes. The Bedouin said, That grain would satisfy me and my family? He said, Yes, and most of your clan. And the Almighty’s saying: Neither cut off nor forbidden means it is not cut off in winter nor summer, rather eating it is continuous and everlasting, no matter what they seek they will find, nothing is forbidden to them by the power of God. Qatada said: No stick, thorn or distance will prevent them from eating it. It was mentioned in the hadith that if a man eats the fruit it will return to its place. And the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches means high, soft and smooth. Al-Nasa’i and Abu ‘Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb told us, Rashdin bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of ‘Umar bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches he said: Its height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between them is five hundred years. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This hadith is hasan gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Rashdin bin Sa’d. He said: Some of the people of knowledge said: The meaning of this hadith is the height of the couches in degrees and the distance between the two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. This is what he said, and this is not known except from the narration of Rashdin bin Sa’d, who is Al-Masry and he is weak. This is what he said. Narrated by Abu Jaafar bin Jarir on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Rushdin on his authority. Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammad, on the authority of Ibn Wahb. Ad-Dhiya’ included it in Sifat al-Jannah from the hadith of Harmalah, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, who said: Diraj told us, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, Abu Mu’awiyah Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Abu Sahl, meaning Katheer ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Hasan: And raised couches means: The height of a couch for a man of the people of Paradise is a journey of eighty years. And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, We created them a special creation, * And made them virgins, * Lovely of equal age, * For the companions of the right hand the pronoun applies to something not mentioned. But since the context, which is the mention of beds, indicates the women who lie on them, He sufficed with that and did not mention them, and the pronoun refers back to them, as in the Almighty’s saying: When there were presented to him in the evening the pure, slender horses, * He said, “Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord, until it was hidden behind the veil.” He means the sun, according to the well-known opinion of the commentators. Al-Akhfash said regarding the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We created them, He implied them and they were not mentioned before that.
