Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati told us, Amr ibn Hashim al-Bayruti told us, Sulayman ibn Abi Karima told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Houris with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: “Houris with wide, white eyes, large eyes. The eyelashes of the houri are like the wings of an eagle.” I said: Tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Like hidden pearls. He said: Their purity is the purity of pearls in shells, untouched by hands. I said: Tell me about His statement: In them are good and beautiful women. He said: Good morals and beautiful faces. I said: Tell me about His statement: As if they were hidden eggs. He said: Their delicacy is like the delicacy of the skin that you see inside an egg, near the shell, which is the gharqa’. I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about His statement: Arab women of equal age. He said: “They are those who were taken in the worldly home as old women, dry-eyed and sun-kissed. God created them after old age, then made them Arab virgins, in love with one another.” Beloved, equal in age, born one day. I said: O Messenger of God, are the women of this world better or the houris? He said: Rather, the women of this world are better than the houris, just as the outer part is better than the lining. I said: O Messenger of God, and how is that? He said: “Because of their prayers, fasting, and worship of God, the Almighty. God has clothed their faces with light and their bodies with silk. They are white in color, green in clothing, yellow in jewelry, their braziers are pearls, and their combs are gold. They say: “We are the immortal ones, so we never die. We are the soft ones, so we never suffer. We are the residents, so we never depart. We are the content ones, so we never become angry. Blessed is he for whom we are and he is for us.” I said: “O Messenger of God, a woman among us marries two, three, or four husbands, then she dies and enters Paradise, and they enter with her. Who will be her husband?” He said: “O Umm Salamah, she is given a choice and chooses the one with the best character, and she says: ‘O Lord, this one had the best character with me, so marry me to him.’ O Umm Salamah, good character takes the best of this world and the hereafter.” In the long and famous hadith of the images, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intercedes for all believers to enter Paradise. God Almighty says, I have interceded for you and given them permission to enter it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, By He who sent me with the truth, you in this world are not more knowledgeable about your wives and your dwellings than the people of Paradise are about their wives and dwellings. A man from among them will enter upon seventy-two wives from among those whom God creates, and two from the children of Adam who have superiority over those whom God created through their worship in this world. He will enter the first of them into a room of ruby on a bed of gold crowned with pearls, upon which will be seventy pairs of fine silk and brocade. He will place his hand between her shoulders, then look at his hand from her chest from behind her clothes, her skin, and her flesh. He will look at the marrow of her leg as one of you looks at a thread in a ruby reed. His liver is a mirror to her, meaning her liver is a mirror to him. While he is with her, he does not get tired of her and she does not get tired of him, and he does not come to her once except that he finds her a virgin. His remembrance does not wane and he does not complain. Before her, except that there is no semen nor any desire. While he is like that, a voice is called out, We know that you do not get tired or bored, except that you have other wives. So he goes out and comes to them one by one. Every time he comes to one, she says, By God, there is nothing in Paradise better than you, and there is nothing in Paradise dearer to me than you. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to him, Will I prostrate in Paradise? He said, Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, prostrate. Then, when he gets up from her, she returns purified and a virgin. Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim bin Jaber, the jurist of Baghdad, narrated to us, Muhammad bin Abdul Malik Al-Daqeeqi Al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ma’la bin Abdul Rahman Al-Wasiti narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Al-Mutawakkil, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the people of Paradise have intercourse with their wives, they will return as virgins. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said: Imran informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The believer will be given such and such strength with regard to wives in Paradise. I said: O Messenger of God, can he do that? He said: He will be given the strength of one hundred. At-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud and said: It is saheeh ghareeb. Abu Al-Qasim At-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Husayn bin Ali Al-Ju’fi, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, will we have intercourse with our wives in Paradise? He said: A man may have intercourse with one hundred virgins in one day. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi said: In my view, this hadith meets the criteria for authenticity, and God knows best. And his saying: Arabs Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means veiled before their husbands. Have you not seen the hyena-camel? It is like that. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Arab women are in love with their husbands and their husbands are in love with them. And this is what Abdullah bin Sarjis, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Yahya bin Abi Katheer, Atiyah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. Thawr bin Yazid said on the authority of Ikrimah that he was asked about his saying: Arabs He said: It is the one who flatters her husband. Shu’bah said on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah: It is coquettishness. Al-Ajlah bin Abdullah said on the authority of Ikrimah: It is shakala. Saleh bin Hayyan said on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah regarding his saying: Arabs He said: Shakala is in the language of the people of Mecca and coquettishness is in the language of the people of Medina. Tamim bin Hudlam said: It is a beautiful wife. Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman said: The Arabs are good speakers. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Sahl ibn Uthman al-Askari, Abu Ali told us on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Arabs - he said - their speech is Arabic. And his saying: of equal age Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning in one age thirty-three years. Mujahid said: of equal age are those of equal status, and in a narration on his authority: similar. Atiyah said: peers. Al-Suddi said: of equal age means in the morals of the two of them, there is no hatred or envy between them, meaning not as they were hostile co-wives. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Kahf, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Muhammad, Arabs of equal age, they said: Those of equal age get along and play together. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a gathering of houris with wide-eyed eyes, who will raise voices the likes of which no creation has ever heard. He said: “They will say, ‘We are immortal, so we will not perish. We are pampered, so we will not be miserable. We are content, so we will not be angry. Blessed is he who is for us and we are for him.’” Then he said: This is a strange hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Ismail bin Umar told us, Ibn Abi Dhi`b told us, on the authority of so-and-so Abdullah bin Rafi`, on the authority of some of the sons of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The houris will sing in Paradise, saying, ‘We are good and beautiful, hidden for noble husbands.’ I said: This Ismail bin Umar is Abu al-Mundhir al-Wasiti, one of the trustworthy and reliable ones. This hadith was narrated by Imam Abdul Rahim bin Ibrahim, nicknamed Duhaim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Awn bin Al-Khattab bin Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The houris will sing in Paradise. We are the beautiful houris, created for noble spouses.” And the Almighty’s statement, for the companions of the right hand, means they were created for the companions of the right hand, or they were saved for the companions of the right hand, or they were married to the companions of the right hand. It is more apparent that it is connected to His statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation, * Then We made them virgins, * Lovely of equal age, * For the companions of the right hand, so its meaning is We created them for the companions of the right hand. This is the interpretation of Ibn Jarir. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Sulayman al-Darani, may God have mercy on him, who said: I prayed one night, then I sat down to supplicate. It was very cold, so I began to supplicate with one hand. Then my eyesight overcame me and I fell asleep. I saw a houri, the likes of whom had never been seen, and she said: O Abu Sulayman, do you supplicate with one hand, while I have been feeding you in bliss for five hundred years? I said: It is possible that his statement: For the companions of the right hand is related to what preceded it, which is his statement: of equal age * For the companions of the right hand meaning in their age, as came in the hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of Jarir on the authority of Ammarah ibn Al-Qa’qa’ on the authority of Abu Zur’ah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be in the image of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be in the light of the brightest shining star in the sky. They do not urinate or defecate, nor do they spit or blow their noses. Their combs will be gold, their sweat will be musk, their censers will be aloe vera, and their wives will be the houris. Their character will be like the character of one man in the image of their father Adam, sixty cubits in the sky.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun and Affan told us, they said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us. Al-Tabarani narrated, and this wording is his, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, beardless, white, curly-haired, and with kohl on their eyes, thirty-three years old. They will be in the form of Adam, sixty cubits tall and seven cubits wide.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Imran al-Qattan, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam, from Muadh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, beardless, and with kohl on their eyes, thirty-three years old. Then he said: Good and strange. Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith told us that Diraj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham on the authority of Abu Sa`id who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies from the people of Paradise, whether young or old, will be returned to Paradise thirty-three years old and will never exceed that, and so will the people of Hellfire. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Suwayd ibn Nasr on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa`d on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith with it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Al-Qasim ibn Hashim told us, Sufyan ibn Salih told us, Rawad ibn Al-Jarrah Al-Asqalani told us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Dhi’ab, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise with the height of Adam, sixty cubits, the king’s cubit! With the beauty of Joseph, and thirty-three years after the birth of Jesus, and with the tongue of Muhammad, hairless, beardless, and kohl-lined.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Mahmud ibn Khalid and Abbas ibn Al-Walid told us: Umar told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Harun ibn Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will be resurrected in the image of Adam, on the birth of Jesus, thirty-three hairless, beardless, and kohl-lined. Then they will be taken to a tree in Paradise and will be clothed by it. Their clothes will not wear out and their youth will not fade.” And the Almighty’s statement: A group of the first peoples * And a group of the last ones means a group of the first ones and a group of the last ones. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Mundhir bin Shadhan told us, Muhammad bin Bakkar told us, Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: Some of them used to take from one another. He said: We were hired one night with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, then we went to him in the morning. He said: “The prophets and their followers were shown to me with their nations. A prophet would pass by me, and a prophet would pass by me in a group! A prophet would be with three people, and a prophet would not be with him.” Qatada recited this verse: Is there not among you a man of sound mind? He said: “Until Moses bin Imran passed by me in a crowd of the Children of Israel. I said: ‘My Lord, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Moses bin Imran and those who followed him from the Children of Israel.’ He said: ‘I said: My Lord, then where are my nation?’ He said: ‘Look to your right in the crowd.’ He said: ‘And if there are faces of men,’ He said: ‘Are you satisfied?’ He said: ‘I am satisfied, my Lord.’ He said: ‘Look to the horizon to your left, and if there are faces of men,’ He said: ‘Are you satisfied?’ I said: ‘I am satisfied, my Lord.’ He said: ‘With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account.’” He said: And Ukasha bin Muhsin from Banu Asad began to speak. Saeed said: He was a Badri man and said: O Prophet of God, supplicate to God to make me one of them. He said: So he said: O God, make him one of them. He said: Another man began to speak and said: O Prophet of God, supplicate to God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you are able, may my father and mother be your ransom, to be among the seventy, then do so. Otherwise, be among the people of the strike. Otherwise, be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen many people gathered around him. Then he said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. So we said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise. He said: So we said: Allahu Akbar. He said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. He said: So we said: Allahu Akbar. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones. He said: So we said among ourselves: Who are these seventy thousand? We said: They are those who were born into Islam and did not associate partners with God. He said: When that reached him, he said: Rather, they are those who do not cauterize, nor seek incantations, nor take omens, and upon their Lord they put their trust. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way through two other chains of narration on the authority of Qatadah, with a similar wording. This hadith has many chains of narration other than this one in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Mihran told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A group from the first and a group from the last. He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: They are both from my nation.
56:32: When God Almighty mentioned the fate of the forerunners, who are the close ones, He followed them by mentioning the companions of the right, who are the righteous, as Maymun ibn Mihran said, the status of the companions of the right is lower than the close ones, so He said, And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right? meaning, who are the companions of the right, what is their state, and what is their fate? Then he explained that, saying, In thornless lote trees. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibn Al-Ahwas, Qasama bin Zuhair, Al-Safar bin Qais, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah bin Kathir, Al-Suddi, Abu Hazra, and others said: It is the one that has no thorns. And from Ibn Abbas: It is the one that is laden with fruit. This is a narration from Ikrimah and Mujahid. And Qatadah also said: We used to say that it is the one that is laden with thorns. And it appears that what is meant is this and that. For the lote tree of this world has many thorns and little fruit, and in the Hereafter, on the contrary, it has no thorns and has many fruits that have weighed down its root, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Salman Al-Najjad said: Muhammad bin Muhammad, he is Al-Baghawi, told us. Hamza bin Abbas told me. Abdullah bin Uthman told us. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us. Safwan bin Amr told us, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions. He said: One day a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned in Paradise a tree that harms…” Its owner, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: What are they? He said: The lote tree, for it has harmful thorns. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘In a lote tree without thorns’? God trimmed its thorns and replaced each thorn with a fruit. It produces fruit, each of which reveals seventy-two types of food, and no color is similar to the other.” Another path Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud said: Muhammad bin Al-Musaffa told us, Muhammad bin Al-Mubarak told us, Yahya bin Hamza told me, Thawr bin Yazid told me, Habib bin Ubaid told me on the authority of Utbah bin Abdul Salami, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, I hear you mention a tree in Paradise, and I do not know of a tree with more thorns than it, meaning the talh tree. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God will place in place of every thorn in it a fruit like the testicle of a groomed goat, in which there are seventy types of food, no color resembling another. And his saying: And talh in layers, talh is a large tree that grows in the land of the Hijaz from the ‘adah tree, the singular of which is talha, and it is a tree with many thorns. Ibn Jarir recited to one of the hadith scholars: Her guide gave her good report and said, Tomorrow you will see the acacia trees and the mountains. Mujahed said: Mandhud means piled up with fruit. This reminds us of the Quraysh because they used to marvel at the shade of the Talh and Sidr trees. Al-Suddi said: Mandhud is masfud. Ibn Abbas said: It resembles the Talh of this world, but its fruit is sweeter than honey. Al-Jawhari said: Talh is a dialect for stalk. I said: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Al-Hasan bin Sa’d from a sheikh from Hamdan who said: I heard Ali say this word about Talh Mandhud. He said: A piled up stalk. Based on this, it is a description of the Sidr, so it is as if he described it as being makhdhud, which means that it has no thorns, and that its stalk is mandhud which means the abundance of its fruit. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Idris, on the authority of Jaafar bin Iyas, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, And Talh Mandhud, meaning bananas. He said: And it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qassama bin Zuhair, Qatadah, and Abu Hazra something similar, and with it. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: And he added and said: The people of Yemen call bananas Talh. Ibn Jarir did not narrate anything other than this statement. And the Almighty’s saying: And an extended shade. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, conveying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing the line. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it likewise from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. And thus Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan on the authority of Falih on his authority, and thus Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and thus Hammad bin Salamah narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Al-Layth bin Saad on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and Aouf on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Hajjaj told us: Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu Ad-Dahhak telling Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for seventy or one hundred years. It is the tree of eternity.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for one hundred years, but he would not be able to cross it. And if you wish, recite: ‘and an extended shade.’” The chain of transmission is good, but they did not include it. Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of `Abdah, `Abd al-Rahim, and al-Bukhari, all on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr, on his authority. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider can travel for a hundred years. Read if you wish: and an extended shade. When that reached Ka’b, he said: He has spoken the truth, by He who sent down the Torah to Moses and the Criterion to Muhammad. If a man were to ride on a tree trunk or a tree stump, then circle around the top of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down in old age. God planted it with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise except that it flows from the base of that tree. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Munhal al-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: and extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Al-Bukhari narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ruh ibn ‘Abd al-Mu’min, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Imran ibn Dawud al-Qattan, on the authority of Qatadah, and in the same way, Muammar and Abu Hilal narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Qatadah. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa’id and Sahl ibn Sa’d, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. This hadith is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and is mutawatir and its authenticity is confirmed by the leading critics of hadith, due to the multiplicity of its chains of transmission, the strength of its isnads, and the trustworthiness of its men. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Abu Hasin narrated to us: We were at a door in a place and with us were Abu Salih and Shuqaiq, meaning Ad-Dhabi. Abu Salih narrated: Abu Hurairah narrated to me: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider would travel for seventy years. Abu Salih said: Do you accuse Abu Hurairah of lying? He said: I do not accuse Abu Hurairah of lying, but I accuse you of lying. This was difficult for the reciters of hadith at that time. I said: Whoever accuses this hadith has invalidated it, even though it is proven and authentic and traced back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tirmidhi said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ziyad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Furat Al-Qazzaz narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no tree in Paradise but its trunk is made of gold. Then he said: Good and strange. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi narrated to us, on the authority of Zam’ah bin Salih, on the authority of Salamah bin Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The extended shade is a tree in Paradise, and its shade is as long as a rider can travel in all its directions, a hundred years. He said: The people of Paradise, the people of the upper rooms and others, will come out to it and converse in its shade. He said: Some of them will desire it and remember the amusement of this world, so God will send a wind from Paradise, and that tree will stir with every amusement in this world. This is a strange narration, its chain of transmission is good, strong, and good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashja’ narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, regarding the verse: and an extended shade, he said: seventy thousand years. Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, similarly. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, and an extended shade, he said: five hundred thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Husayn ibn Nafi’ told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Auf said, on the authority of al-Hasan: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Shabib said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In Paradise there are trees that cannot be carried to shelter oneself under them. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Hazra said regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, that is, it does not end, there is no sun or heat in it like before dawn. Ibn Mas’ud said: Paradise is covered with curtains like the time between dawn and sunrise. Verses have come before, such as the statement of God, the Most High: And We will admit them into a deep shade, and His statement: Its food is everlasting and its shade, and His statement: In shades and springs, and other verses. And His statement: God the Almighty said: And flowing water. Al-Thawri said: It flows without a trench. We have already discussed the interpretation of God the Almighty’s statement: Therein are rivers of water that is not stagnant, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And the Almighty said: And abundant fruit, neither forbidden nor forbidden. That is, they will have abundant fruits of various colors that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as the Almighty said: Whenever they are provided with fruit therefrom as provision, they say, ‘This is what we were provided with before.’ And they will be given it in resemblance. That is, the shape resembles the shape, but the taste is different. And in the two Sahihs, when mentioning the lote tree of the farthest boundary, it says: Then behold, its leaves are like the ears of elephants, and its dates are like the jars of Hajar. And in them also from the hadith of Malik from Zaid from Ata’ ibn Yasar from Ibn Abbas who said: The sun eclipsed and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed and the people were with him and he mentioned the prayer, and in it they said: O Messenger of God, we saw you reach for something in this place of yours and then we saw you slump down, he said: I saw Paradise and reached for a bunch of grapes from it, and if I had taken it you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained. And Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Abdullah ibn Ja’far told us, Ubaydullah told us, Ibn Aqil told us from Jabir who said: While we were praying the noon prayer, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward and we moved forward with him, then he reached for something to take it and then he stepped back, and when he had finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: O Messenger of God, today you did something in the prayer that you did not do, he said: “Paradise and what is in it of flowers and freshness were shown to me, and I reached for a bunch of grapes from it to bring it to you, but I was prevented from it, and if I brought it to you, I would eat from it from between the sky and the earth and it would not be diminished.” And Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Bahr told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about the Cistern. He mentioned Paradise, then the Bedouin said: Is there fruit in it? He said: Yes, and in it is a tree called Tuba. He said: Then he mentioned something, but I do not know what it was. He said: What tree of our land does it resemble? He said: It does not resemble any of the trees of your land? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you been to Syria? He said: No. He said: “It resembles a tree in Syria called al-Jawzah. It grows on one stem and its top is spread out.” He said: How big is the cluster? He said: A month’s journey for the speckled crow that does not stop. He said: How big is its root? He said: If a young camel from your family were to set out on a journey, it would not reach its root until its collarbone would break from old age. He said: In it are grapes? He said: Yes. He said: How big is the seed? He said, Did your father ever slaughter a large goat from his flock? He said, Yes. He said, He skinned its hide and gave it to your mother and said, 'Make us a bucket from it?' He said, Yes. The Bedouin said, That grain would satisfy me and my family? He said, Yes, and most of your clan. And the Almighty’s saying: Neither cut off nor forbidden means it is not cut off in winter nor summer, rather eating it is continuous and everlasting, no matter what they seek they will find, nothing is forbidden to them by the power of God. Qatada said: No stick, thorn or distance will prevent them from eating it. It was mentioned in the hadith that if a man eats the fruit it will return to its place. And the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches means high, soft and smooth. Al-Nasa’i and Abu ‘Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb told us, Rashdin bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of ‘Umar bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches he said: Its height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between them is five hundred years. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This hadith is hasan gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Rashdin bin Sa’d. He said: Some of the people of knowledge said: The meaning of this hadith is the height of the couches in degrees and the distance between the two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. This is what he said, and this is not known except from the narration of Rashdin bin Sa’d, who is Al-Masry and he is weak. This is what he said. Narrated by Abu Jaafar bin Jarir on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Rushdin on his authority. Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammad, on the authority of Ibn Wahb. Ad-Dhiya’ included it in Sifat al-Jannah from the hadith of Harmalah, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, who said: Diraj told us, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, Abu Mu’awiyah Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Abu Sahl, meaning Katheer ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Hasan: And raised couches means: The height of a couch for a man of the people of Paradise is a journey of eighty years. And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, We created them a special creation, * And made them virgins, * Lovely of equal age, * For the companions of the right hand the pronoun applies to something not mentioned. But since the context, which is the mention of beds, indicates the women who lie on them, He sufficed with that and did not mention them, and the pronoun refers back to them, as in the Almighty’s saying: When there were presented to him in the evening the pure, slender horses, * He said, “Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord, until it was hidden behind the veil.” He means the sun, according to the well-known opinion of the commentators. Al-Akhfash said regarding the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We created them, He implied them and they were not mentioned before that. Abu Ubaidah said: They were mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: And fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes, * Like hidden pearls. So the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We created them, means We restored them in the other creation after they were old, bleary-eyed women. They became pure virgins, meaning after marriage they returned to pure virgins, endeared to their husbands with sweetness, charm, and beauty. Some of them said Arabs, meaning ghanjat. Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi said, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Indeed, We created them, meaning old women who were blind and lame in this world. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange, and Musa and Yazid are weak. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Auf al-Himsi told us, Adam told us, meaning Ibn Abi Iyas, Shaiban bin Jabir told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Murrah, on the authority of Salamah bin Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say regarding the verse: Indeed, We created them a special creation, meaning the previously married and the virgins who were in this world. Abd bin Hamid said: Mus`ab bin Muqdam told us, al-Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: An old woman came and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to admit me to Paradise. He said: O mother of so-and-so, an old woman will not enter Paradise. She turned away crying. He said: “Tell her that she will not enter it while she is old, for God Almighty says: ‘Indeed, We created them a special creation * And made them virgins’.” Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Al-Shama’il on the authority of Abd bin Hamid. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati told us, Amr ibn Hashim al-Bayruti told us, Sulayman ibn Abi Karima told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Houris with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: “Houris with wide, white eyes, large eyes. The eyelashes of the houri are like the wings of an eagle.” I said: Tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Like hidden pearls. He said: Their purity is the purity of pearls in shells, untouched by hands. I said: Tell me about His statement: In them are good and beautiful women. He said: Good morals and beautiful faces. I said: Tell me about His statement: As if they were hidden eggs. He said: Their delicacy is like the delicacy of the skin that you see inside an egg, near the shell, which is the gharqa’. I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about His statement: Arab women of equal age. He said: “They are those who were taken in the worldly home as old women, dry-eyed and sun-kissed. God created them after old age, then made them Arab virgins, in love with one another.” Beloved, equal in age, born one day. I said: O Messenger of God, are the women of this world better or the houris? He said: Rather, the women of this world are better than the houris, just as the outer part is better than the lining. I said: O Messenger of God, and how is that? He said: “Because of their prayers, fasting, and worship of God, the Almighty. God has clothed their faces with light and their bodies with silk. They are white in color, green in clothing, yellow in jewelry, their braziers are pearls, and their combs are gold. They say: “We are the immortal ones, so we never die. We are the soft ones, so we never suffer. We are the residents, so we never depart. We are the content ones, so we never become angry. Blessed is he for whom we are and he is for us.” I said: “O Messenger of God, a woman among us marries two, three, or four husbands, then she dies and enters Paradise, and they enter with her. Who will be her husband?” He said: “O Umm Salamah, she is given a choice and chooses the one with the best character, and she says: ‘O Lord, this one had the best character with me, so marry me to him.’ O Umm Salamah, good character takes the best of this world and the hereafter.” In the long and famous hadith of the images, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intercedes for all believers to enter Paradise. God Almighty says, I have interceded for you and given them permission to enter it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, By He who sent me with the truth, you in this world are not more knowledgeable about your wives and your dwellings than the people of Paradise are about their wives and dwellings. A man from among them will enter upon seventy-two wives from among those whom God creates, and two from the children of Adam who have superiority over those whom God created through their worship in this world. He will enter the first of them into a room of ruby on a bed of gold crowned with pearls, upon which will be seventy pairs of fine silk and brocade. He will place his hand between her shoulders, then look at his hand from her chest from behind her clothes, her skin, and her flesh. He will look at the marrow of her leg as one of you looks at a thread in a ruby reed. His liver is a mirror to her, meaning her liver is a mirror to him. While he is with her, he does not get tired of her and she does not get tired of him, and he does not come to her once except that he finds her a virgin. His remembrance does not wane and he does not complain. Before her, except that there is no semen nor any desire. While he is like that, a voice is called out, We know that you do not get tired or bored, except that you have other wives. So he goes out and comes to them one by one. Every time he comes to one, she says, By God, there is nothing in Paradise better than you, and there is nothing in Paradise dearer to me than you. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to him, Will I prostrate in Paradise? He said, Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, prostrate. Then, when he gets up from her, she returns purified and a virgin. Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim bin Jaber, the jurist of Baghdad, narrated to us, Muhammad bin Abdul Malik Al-Daqeeqi Al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ma’la bin Abdul Rahman Al-Wasiti narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Al-Mutawakkil, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the people of Paradise have intercourse with their wives, they will return as virgins. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said: Imran informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The believer will be given such and such strength with regard to wives in Paradise. I said: O Messenger of God, can he do that? He said: He will be given the strength of one hundred. At-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud and said: It is saheeh ghareeb. Abu Al-Qasim At-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Husayn bin Ali Al-Ju’fi, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, will we have intercourse with our wives in Paradise? He said: A man may have intercourse with one hundred virgins in one day. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi said: In my view, this hadith meets the criteria for authenticity, and God knows best. And his saying: Arabs Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means veiled before their husbands. Have you not seen the hyena-camel? It is like that. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Arab women are in love with their husbands and their husbands are in love with them. And this is what Abdullah bin Sarjis, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Yahya bin Abi Katheer, Atiyah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. Thawr bin Yazid said on the authority of Ikrimah that he was asked about his saying: Arabs He said: It is the one who flatters her husband. Shu’bah said on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah: It is coquettishness. Al-Ajlah bin Abdullah said on the authority of Ikrimah: It is shakala. Saleh bin Hayyan said on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah regarding his saying: Arabs He said: Shakala is in the language of the people of Mecca and coquettishness is in the language of the people of Medina. Tamim bin Hudlam said: It is a beautiful wife. Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman said: The Arabs are good speakers. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Sahl ibn Uthman al-Askari, Abu Ali told us on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Arabs - he said - their speech is Arabic. And his saying: of equal age Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning in one age thirty-three years. Mujahid said: of equal age are those of equal status, and in a narration on his authority: similar. Atiyah said: peers. Al-Suddi said: of equal age means in the morals of the two of them, there is no hatred or envy between them, meaning not as they were hostile co-wives. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Kahf, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Muhammad, Arabs of equal age, they said: Those of equal age get along and play together. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a gathering of houris with wide-eyed eyes, who will raise voices the likes of which no creation has ever heard. He said: “They will say, ‘We are immortal, so we will not perish. We are pampered, so we will not be miserable. We are content, so we will not be angry. Blessed is he who is for us and we are for him.’” Then he said: This is a strange hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Ismail bin Umar told us, Ibn Abi Dhi`b told us, on the authority of so-and-so Abdullah bin Rafi`, on the authority of some of the sons of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The houris will sing in Paradise, saying, ‘We are good and beautiful, hidden for noble husbands.’ I said: This Ismail bin Umar is Abu al-Mundhir al-Wasiti, one of the trustworthy and reliable ones. This hadith was narrated by Imam Abdul Rahim bin Ibrahim, nicknamed Duhaim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Awn bin Al-Khattab bin Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The houris will sing in Paradise. We are the beautiful houris, created for noble spouses.” And the Almighty’s statement, for the companions of the right hand, means they were created for the companions of the right hand, or they were saved for the companions of the right hand, or they were married to the companions of the right hand. It is more apparent that it is connected to His statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation, * Then We made them virgins, * Lovely of equal age, * For the companions of the right hand, so its meaning is We created them for the companions of the right hand. This is the interpretation of Ibn Jarir. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Sulayman al-Darani, may God have mercy on him, who said: I prayed one night, then I sat down to supplicate. It was very cold, so I began to supplicate with one hand. Then my eyesight overcame me and I fell asleep. I saw a houri, the likes of whom had never been seen, and she said: O Abu Sulayman, do you supplicate with one hand, while I have been feeding you in bliss for five hundred years? I said: It is possible that his statement: For the companions of the right hand is related to what preceded it, which is his statement: of equal age * For the companions of the right hand meaning in their age, as came in the hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of Jarir on the authority of Ammarah ibn Al-Qa’qa’ on the authority of Abu Zur’ah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be in the image of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be in the light of the brightest shining star in the sky. They do not urinate or defecate, nor do they spit or blow their noses. Their combs will be gold, their sweat will be musk, their censers will be aloe vera, and their wives will be the houris. Their character will be like the character of one man in the image of their father Adam, sixty cubits in the sky.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun and Affan told us, they said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us. Al-Tabarani narrated, and this wording is his, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, beardless, white, curly-haired, and with kohl on their eyes, thirty-three years old. They will be in the form of Adam, sixty cubits tall and seven cubits wide.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Imran al-Qattan, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam, from Muadh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, beardless, and with kohl on their eyes, thirty-three years old. Then he said: Good and strange. Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith told us that Diraj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham on the authority of Abu Sa`id who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies from the people of Paradise, whether young or old, will be returned to Paradise thirty-three years old and will never exceed that, and so will the people of Hellfire. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Suwayd ibn Nasr on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa`d on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith with it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Al-Qasim ibn Hashim told us, Sufyan ibn Salih told us, Rawad ibn Al-Jarrah Al-Asqalani told us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Dhi’ab, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise with the height of Adam, sixty cubits, the king’s cubit! With the beauty of Joseph, and thirty-three years after the birth of Jesus, and with the tongue of Muhammad, hairless, beardless, and kohl-lined.” Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Mahmud ibn Khalid and Abbas ibn Al-Walid told us: Umar told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Harun ibn Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will be resurrected in the image of Adam, on the birth of Jesus, thirty-three hairless, beardless, and kohl-lined. Then they will be taken to a tree in Paradise and will be clothed by it. Their clothes will not wear out and their youth will not fade.” And the Almighty’s statement: A group of the first peoples * And a group of the last ones means a group of the first ones and a group of the last ones. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Mundhir bin Shadhan told us, Muhammad bin Bakkar told us, Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: Some of them used to take from one another. He said: We were hired one night with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, then we went to him in the morning. He said: “The prophets and their followers were shown to me with their nations. A prophet would pass by me, and a prophet would pass by me in a group! A prophet would be with three people, and a prophet would not be with him.” Qatada recited this verse: Is there not among you a man of sound mind? He said: “Until Moses bin Imran passed by me in a crowd of the Children of Israel. I said: ‘My Lord, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Moses bin Imran and those who followed him from the Children of Israel.’ He said: ‘I said: My Lord, then where are my nation?’ He said: ‘Look to your right in the crowd.’ He said: ‘And if there are faces of men,’ He said: ‘Are you satisfied?’ He said: ‘I am satisfied, my Lord.’ He said: ‘Look to the horizon to your left, and if there are faces of men,’ He said: ‘Are you satisfied?’ I said: ‘I am satisfied, my Lord.’ He said: ‘With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account.’” He said: And Ukasha bin Muhsin from Banu Asad began to speak. Saeed said: He was a Badri man and said: O Prophet of God, supplicate to God to make me one of them. He said: So he said: O God, make him one of them. He said: Another man began to speak and said: O Prophet of God, supplicate to God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you are able, may my father and mother be your ransom, to be among the seventy, then do so. Otherwise, be among the people of the strike. Otherwise, be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen many people gathered around him. Then he said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. So we said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise. He said: So we said: Allahu Akbar. He said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. He said: So we said: Allahu Akbar. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: A group of the first ones * And a group of the last ones. He said: So we said among ourselves: Who are these seventy thousand? We said: They are those who were born into Islam and did not associate partners with God. He said: When that reached him, he said: Rather, they are those who do not cauterize, nor seek incantations, nor take omens, and upon their Lord they put their trust. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way through two other chains of narration on the authority of Qatadah, with a similar wording. This hadith has many chains of narration other than this one in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Mihran told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A group from the first and a group from the last. He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: They are both from my nation.
56:33: When God Almighty mentioned the fate of the forerunners, who are the close ones, He followed them by mentioning the companions of the right, who are the righteous, as Maymun ibn Mihran said, the status of the companions of the right is lower than the close ones, so He said, And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right? meaning, who are the companions of the right, what is their state, and what is their fate? Then he explained that, saying, In thornless lote trees. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibn Al-Ahwas, Qasama bin Zuhair, Al-Safar bin Qais, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah bin Kathir, Al-Suddi, Abu Hazra, and others said: It is the one that has no thorns. And from Ibn Abbas: It is the one that is laden with fruit. This is a narration from Ikrimah and Mujahid. And Qatadah also said: We used to say that it is the one that is laden with thorns. And it appears that what is meant is this and that. For the lote tree of this world has many thorns and little fruit, and in the Hereafter, on the contrary, it has no thorns and has many fruits that have weighed down its root, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Salman Al-Najjad said: Muhammad bin Muhammad, he is Al-Baghawi, told us. Hamza bin Abbas told me. Abdullah bin Uthman told us. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us. Safwan bin Amr told us, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions. He said: One day a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned in Paradise a tree that harms…” Its owner, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: What are they? He said: The lote tree, for it has harmful thorns. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘In a lote tree without thorns’? God trimmed its thorns and replaced each thorn with a fruit. It produces fruit, each of which reveals seventy-two types of food, and no color is similar to the other.” Another path Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud said: Muhammad bin Al-Musaffa told us, Muhammad bin Al-Mubarak told us, Yahya bin Hamza told me, Thawr bin Yazid told me, Habib bin Ubaid told me on the authority of Utbah bin Abdul Salami, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, I hear you mention a tree in Paradise, and I do not know of a tree with more thorns than it, meaning the talh tree. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God will place in place of every thorn in it a fruit like the testicle of a groomed goat, in which there are seventy types of food, no color resembling another. And his saying: And talh in layers, talh is a large tree that grows in the land of the Hijaz from the ‘adah tree, the singular of which is talha, and it is a tree with many thorns. Ibn Jarir recited to one of the hadith scholars: Her guide gave her good report and said, Tomorrow you will see the acacia trees and the mountains. Mujahed said: Mandhud means piled up with fruit. This reminds us of the Quraysh because they used to marvel at the shade of the Talh and Sidr trees. Al-Suddi said: Mandhud is masfud. Ibn Abbas said: It resembles the Talh of this world, but its fruit is sweeter than honey. Al-Jawhari said: Talh is a dialect for stalk. I said: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Al-Hasan bin Sa’d from a sheikh from Hamdan who said: I heard Ali say this word about Talh Mandhud. He said: A piled up stalk. Based on this, it is a description of the Sidr, so it is as if he described it as being makhdhud, which means that it has no thorns, and that its stalk is mandhud which means the abundance of its fruit. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Idris, on the authority of Jaafar bin Iyas, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, And Talh Mandhud, meaning bananas. He said: And it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qassama bin Zuhair, Qatadah, and Abu Hazra something similar, and with it. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: And he added and said: The people of Yemen call bananas Talh. Ibn Jarir did not narrate anything other than this statement. And the Almighty’s saying: And an extended shade. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, conveying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing the line. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Muslim narrated it likewise from the hadith of al-A’raj with it. And thus Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan on the authority of Falih on his authority, and thus Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and thus Hammad bin Salamah narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Al-Layth bin Saad on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and Aouf on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Hajjaj told us: Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu Ad-Dahhak telling Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for seventy or one hundred years. It is the tree of eternity.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for one hundred years, but he would not be able to cross it. And if you wish, recite: ‘and an extended shade.’” The chain of transmission is good, but they did not include it. Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of `Abdah, `Abd al-Rahim, and al-Bukhari, all on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Amr, on his authority. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider can travel for a hundred years. Read if you wish: and an extended shade. When that reached Ka’b, he said: He has spoken the truth, by He who sent down the Torah to Moses and the Criterion to Muhammad. If a man were to ride on a tree trunk or a tree stump, then circle around the top of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down in old age. God planted it with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise except that it flows from the base of that tree. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Munhal al-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: and extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Al-Bukhari narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ruh ibn ‘Abd al-Mu’min, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Imran ibn Dawud al-Qattan, on the authority of Qatadah, and in the same way, Muammar and Abu Hilal narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Qatadah. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa’id and Sahl ibn Sa’d, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree, in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. This hadith is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and is mutawatir and its authenticity is confirmed by the leading critics of hadith, due to the multiplicity of its chains of transmission, the strength of its isnads, and the trustworthiness of its men. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Abu Hasin narrated to us: We were at a door in a place and with us were Abu Salih and Shuqaiq, meaning Ad-Dhabi. Abu Salih narrated: Abu Hurairah narrated to me: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider would travel for seventy years. Abu Salih said: Do you accuse Abu Hurairah of lying? He said: I do not accuse Abu Hurairah of lying, but I accuse you of lying. This was difficult for the reciters of hadith at that time. I said: Whoever accuses this hadith has invalidated it, even though it is proven and authentic and traced back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tirmidhi said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ziyad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Furat Al-Qazzaz narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no tree in Paradise but its trunk is made of gold. Then he said: Good and strange. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi narrated to us, on the authority of Zam’ah bin Salih, on the authority of Salamah bin Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The extended shade is a tree in Paradise, and its shade is as long as a rider can travel in all its directions, a hundred years. He said: The people of Paradise, the people of the upper rooms and others, will come out to it and converse in its shade. He said: Some of them will desire it and remember the amusement of this world, so God will send a wind from Paradise, and that tree will stir with every amusement in this world. This is a strange narration, its chain of transmission is good, strong, and good. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id Al-Ashja’ narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, regarding the verse: and an extended shade, he said: seventy thousand years. Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, similarly. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, and an extended shade, he said: five hundred thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Husayn ibn Nafi’ told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Auf said, on the authority of al-Hasan: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Shabib said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In Paradise there are trees that cannot be carried to shelter oneself under them. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Hazra said regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And extended shade, that is, it does not end, there is no sun or heat in it like before dawn. Ibn Mas’ud said: Paradise is covered with curtains like the time between dawn and sunrise. Verses have come before, such as the statement of God, the Most High: And We will admit them into a deep shade, and His statement: Its food is everlasting and its shade, and His statement: In shades and springs, and other verses. And His statement: God the Almighty said: And flowing water. Al-Thawri said: It flows without a trench. We have already discussed the interpretation of God the Almighty’s statement: Therein are rivers of water that is not stagnant, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And the Almighty said: And abundant fruit, neither forbidden nor forbidden. That is, they will have abundant fruits of various colors that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as the Almighty said: Whenever they are provided with fruit therefrom as provision, they say, ‘This is what we were provided with before.’ And they will be given it in resemblance. That is, the shape resembles the shape, but the taste is different. And in the two Sahihs, when mentioning the lote tree of the farthest boundary, it says: Then behold, its leaves are like the ears of elephants, and its dates are like the jars of Hajar. And in them also from the hadith of Malik from Zaid from Ata’ ibn Yasar from Ibn Abbas who said: The sun eclipsed and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed and the people were with him and he mentioned the prayer, and in it they said: O Messenger of God, we saw you reach for something in this place of yours and then we saw you slump down, he said: I saw Paradise and reached for a bunch of grapes from it, and if I had taken it you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained. And Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Abu Khaithama told us, Abdullah ibn Ja’far told us, Ubaydullah told us, Ibn Aqil told us from Jabir who said: While we were praying the noon prayer, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward and we moved forward with him, then he reached for something to take it and then he stepped back, and when he had finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: O Messenger of God, today you did something in the prayer that you did not do, he said: “Paradise and what is in it of flowers and freshness were shown to me, and I reached for a bunch of grapes from it to bring it to you, but I was prevented from it, and if I brought it to you, I would eat from it from between the sky and the earth and it would not be diminished.” And Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu Al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Bahr told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about the Cistern. He mentioned Paradise, then the Bedouin said: Is there fruit in it? He said: Yes, and in it is a tree called Tuba. He said: Then he mentioned something, but I do not know what it was. He said: What tree of our land does it resemble? He said: It does not resemble any of the trees of your land? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you been to Syria? He said: No. He said: “It resembles a tree in Syria called al-Jawzah. It grows on one stem and its top is spread out.” He said: How big is the cluster? He said: A month’s journey for the speckled crow that does not stop. He said: How big is its root? He said: If a young camel from your family were to set out on a journey, it would not reach its root until its collarbone would break from old age. He said: In it are grapes? He said: Yes. He said: How big is the seed? He said, Did your father ever slaughter a large goat from his flock? He said, Yes. He said, He skinned its hide and gave it to your mother and said, 'Make us a bucket from it?' He said, Yes. The Bedouin said, That grain would satisfy me and my family? He said, Yes, and most of your clan. And the Almighty’s saying: Neither cut off nor forbidden means it is not cut off in winter nor summer, rather eating it is continuous and everlasting, no matter what they seek they will find, nothing is forbidden to them by the power of God. Qatada said: No stick, thorn or distance will prevent them from eating it. It was mentioned in the hadith that if a man eats the fruit it will return to its place. And the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches means high, soft and smooth. Al-Nasa’i and Abu ‘Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb told us, Rashdin bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of ‘Umar bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And raised couches he said: Its height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between them is five hundred years. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This hadith is hasan gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Rashdin bin Sa’d. He said: Some of the people of knowledge said: The meaning of this hadith is the height of the couches in degrees and the distance between the two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. This is what he said, and this is not known except from the narration of Rashdin bin Sa’d, who is Al-Masry and he is weak. This is what he said. Narrated by Abu Jaafar bin Jarir on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Rushdin on his authority. Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammad, on the authority of Ibn Wahb. Ad-Dhiya’ included it in Sifat al-Jannah from the hadith of Harmalah, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, who said: Diraj told us, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, Abu Mu’awiyah Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Abu Sahl, meaning Katheer ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Hasan: And raised couches means: The height of a couch for a man of the people of Paradise is a journey of eighty years. And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, We created them a special creation, * And made them virgins, * Lovely of equal age, * For the companions of the right hand the pronoun applies to something not mentioned. But since the context, which is the mention of beds, indicates the women who lie on them, He sufficed with that and did not mention them, and the pronoun refers back to them, as in the Almighty’s saying: When there were presented to him in the evening the pure, slender horses, * He said, “Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord, until it was hidden behind the veil.” He means the sun, according to the well-known opinion of the commentators. Al-Akhfash said regarding the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We created them, He implied them and they were not mentioned before that. Abu Ubaidah said: They were mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: And fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes, * Like hidden pearls. So the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We created them, means We restored them in the other creation after they were old, bleary-eyed women. They became pure virgins, meaning after marriage they returned to pure virgins, endeared to their husbands with sweetness, charm, and beauty. Some of them said Arabs, meaning ghanjat. Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi said, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Indeed, We created them, meaning old women who were blind and lame in this world. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange, and Musa and Yazid are weak. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Auf al-Himsi told us, Adam told us, meaning Ibn Abi Iyas, Shaiban bin Jabir told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Murrah, on the authority of Salamah bin Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say regarding the verse: Indeed, We created them a special creation, meaning the previously married and the virgins who were in this world. Abd bin Hamid said: Mus`ab bin Muqdam told us, al-Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: An old woman came and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to admit me to Paradise. He said: O mother of so-and-so, an old woman will not enter Paradise. She turned away crying. He said: “Tell her that she will not enter it while she is old, for God Almighty says: ‘Indeed, We created them a special creation * And made them virgins’.” Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Al-Shama’il on the authority of Abd bin Hamid. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati told us, Amr ibn Hashim al-Bayruti told us, Sulayman ibn Abi Karima told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Houris with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: “Houris with wide, white eyes, large eyes. The eyelashes of the houri are like the wings of an eagle.” I said: Tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Like hidden pearls. He said: Their purity is the purity of pearls in shells, untouched by hands. I said: Tell me about His statement: In them are good and beautiful women. He said: Good morals and beautiful faces. I said: Tell me about His statement: As if they were hidden eggs. He said: Their delicacy is like the delicacy of the skin that you see inside an egg, near the shell, which is the gharqa’.
