This which Qatada sent was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, and he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “This fire of yours is a part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell, and it was struck with the sea twice. Were it not for that, God would not have made any benefit in it for anyone.” Imam Malik said, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The fire of the children of Adam that they kindle is a part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. They said: O Messenger of God, is that sufficient? He said: It has been preferred over it by sixty-nine parts. Narrated by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Malik, and by Muslim from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with this wording. In another version: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it has been preferred over it by sixty-nine parts, each of them like… Its heat.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Amr al-Khalal told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami told us, Ma’n ibn Isa al-Fazar told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of his uncle Abu Sahl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what this fire of yours is like in comparison to the fire of Hell? It is seventy times blacker than this fire of yours. Al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi said: Abu Mus’ab narrated it on the authority of Malik, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet, and in my view it meets the criteria for authenticity. And the Almighty’s saying: And provision for the needy. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Nadr ibn Arabi said: By the needy, he means travelers. Ibn Jarir chose this and said: And from it is their saying, The house has been destroyed, when its people have departed. And someone else said: The qayy and the qawwa’ are the deserted, empty, and far from civilization. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The one who is strengthened here is the hungry one. Layth ibn Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid: And provision for the strengthened, for the resident and the traveler for every food that can only be prepared with fire. Sufyan narrated this on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: His statement: For the strengthened means those who enjoy themselves from all people. This was also mentioned on the authority of Ikrimah. This interpretation is more general than others, for the resident and the traveler, rich and poor, all need it for cooking, warming themselves, lighting, and other benefits. Then it is from the kindness of God the Most High that He deposited it in stones and pure iron so that the traveler can carry it in his belongings and among his clothes. So if he needs that in his home, he takes out his flint, kindles, and lights his fire, so he cooks with it, warms himself with it, and roasts, and finds comfort in it and benefits from it in all other ways. For this reason, He singled out travelers, even though this is general for all people! This may be proven by what Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Abu Khidash Habban ibn Zayd al-Shar’i’ al-Shami on the authority of a man from the Muhajirun of Qarn that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Muslims are partners in three things: fire, pasture, and water.” Ibn Majah narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three things should not be forbidden: water, pasture, and fire.” He also has an addition from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this, and its price is forbidden, but in its chain of transmission is Abdullah ibn Kharash ibn Hawshab, who is weak, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great, meaning the One by whose power He created these different and opposite things: pure, fresh, cold water, and if He had willed, He could have made it salty and bitter like the flooding seas. And He created the burning fire and made that a benefit for the servants, and made this a benefit for them in their worldly life and a deterrent for them in the afterlife.
56:75: Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: God the Almighty does not swear by any of His creation, but rather it is an opening with which He begins His speech. This statement is weak, and the majority are of the opinion that it is an oath from God, who swears by whatever He wills of His creation, and it is evidence of His greatness. Then some of the commentators said: The la here is redundant, and its meaning is that He swore by the positions of the stars. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, and its answer would be: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an. Others said: The la is not redundant and has no meaning, but rather it is used at the beginning of the oath if it is sworn by something negative, like the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: No, by God, the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman. And so here the meaning of the speech is: I do not swear by the positions of the stars. The matter is not as you claimed in the Qur’an, that it is magic or divination, but rather it is a noble Qur’an. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the Arab scholars said: The meaning of his statement, So I swear is that the matter is not as you say. Then he resumed the oath after that, and it was said that he swore. They differed over the meaning of his statement, By the positions of the stars. Hakim ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the stars of the Qur'an, for it was revealed all at once on the Night of Decree from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven, then it was revealed in parts over the years after that. Then Ibn Abbas recited this verse. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Qur'an was revealed all at once from God from the Preserved Tablet to the noble recording angels in the lowest heaven. The angels recorded it for Gabriel over twenty nights, and Gabriel recorded it for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for twenty years. So his statement, So I swear by the positions of the stars is the stars of the Qur'an. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, As-Suddi, and Abu Hazra said. Mujahid also said: The positions of the stars in the sky, and it is said their risings and their risings. And this is what Al-Hasan and Qatada said, and this is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir. From Qatada: Its locations are its dwellings. From Al-Hasan also: What is meant by this is its scattering on the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said, So I swear by the positions of the stars, meaning the stars, which when the people of the Jahiliyyah were given rain, they would say: We had rain because of such and such a star. And His statement, And indeed, it is an oath, if you but knew, a great one, means, this oath by which I have sworn is a great oath. If you knew its greatness, you would magnify the one being sworn by. Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an, meaning, this Qur’an that was revealed to Muhammad is a great book. In a protected book, meaning, respected, in a great, preserved, and honored book. Ibn Jarir said, Ismail bin Musa told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Hakim, who is Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. None shall touch it except the purified, he said: The book that is in the heaven. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, None shall touch it except the purified ones, meaning the angels. This is what Anas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Jabir bin Zaid, Abu Nahik, Al-Suddi, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, and others said. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, None shall touch it except the purified, he said: None shall touch it with God except the purified. As for in this world, it is the impure Magians and the unclean hypocrites who touch it. He said: In Ibn Mas’ud’s reading, it is: None shall touch it except the purified. Abu al-A’liyah said: None shall touch it except the purified, not you, you are the people of sins. Ibn Zayd said: The infidels of Quraysh claimed that this Qur’an was revealed by the devils, so God the Most High informed us that none shall touch it except the purified, as He the Most High said: “And it was not brought down by the devils. And it is not for them, nor are they able. Indeed, they are removed from hearing.” This statement is a good statement, and it does not deviate from the statements that preceded it. Al-Farra’ said: None will find its taste and benefit except the one who believes in it. Others said, None shall touch it except those who are pure, meaning from major ritual impurity or ritual impurity. They said, The wording of the verse is a statement, but its meaning is a request. They said, “What is meant by the Qur’an here is the Mushaf, as Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade traveling with the Qur’an to the land of the enemy for fear that the enemy might obtain it.” They cited as evidence for that what Imam Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm that in the letter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to Amr bin Hazm that none shall touch the Qur’an except the pure. Abu Dawud narrated in Al-Marasil from the hadith of Al-Zuhri who said: I read in a document with Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: None shall touch the Qur’an except one who is pure. This is a good and reliable hadith that was read by Al-Zuhri and others, and something like this should be accepted. Ad-Daraqutni narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Hazm, Abdullah bin Umar, and Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas, and there is a problem with the chain of transmission of each of them. And God knows best. And the statement of God, A revelation from the Lord of the worlds means that this Qur’an was revealed by God, Lord of the worlds, and it is not as they say that it is magic, soothsaying, or poetry. Rather, it is the truth about which there is no doubt, and there is no beneficial truth beyond it. And the Almighty’s saying: Is it then that you are in denial of this narration? Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That is, you are denying and not believing it. Ad-Dahhak, Abu Hazra, and As-Suddi said the same. Mujahid said: In denial means you want to agree with them in it and rely on them. And you make your provision that you lie. Some of them said: The meaning of And you make your provision is your thanks that you lie, meaning you lie instead of thanks. It was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas that they read it as And you make your provision that you lie, as will come. Ibn Jarir said: It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Haytham Ibn Adi that from the language of Azdshanu’ah is what someone has been provided with meaning what someone has been thankful for. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-A'la, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: And you make your provision say, 'Your gratitude is that you lie,' and you say, 'We received rain because of such and such a star, because of such and such a star.' This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Makhul ibn Ibrahim al-Nahdi, and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, and on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Bakr, all three of them on the authority of Isra'il, with it as a marfu' hadith. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Mani', on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad who is al-Marwazi, with it as a hasan gharib hadith. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abd al-A'la, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: No people ever receive rain except that some of them become disbelievers in the morning, saying, 'We received rain because of such and such a star.'" Ibn Abbas recited: And you make your provision that you deny. This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Ibn Abbas. Malik said in Al-Muwatta’ from Salih ibn Kaysan from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas’ud from Zayd ibn Khalid Al-Juhani that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) led us in the dawn prayer at Al-Hudaibiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said: Do you know what your Lord has said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “He said: ‘Among My servants there have become some who believe in Me and some who disbelieve. As for he who says, “We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of God,” he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. As for he who says, We have been given rain because of such-and-such a star, he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i, all from the hadith of Malik. Muslim said: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi and Amr ibn Sawad told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told us, Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: “God does not send down a blessing from the sky except that a group of people disbelieve in it in the morning. Rain comes down and they say, ‘It is because of such and such a star.’” Muslim is the only one to narrate it from this chain of narration. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God may grant a people a blessing in the morning or in the evening, and some people disbelieve in it in the morning, and they say, ‘We were given rain because of such and such a star.’ Muhammad said: He is Ibn Ibrahim. I mentioned this hadith to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: “We have heard it from Abu Hurayrah, and someone told me that he witnessed ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him praying for rain. When he prayed for rain, he turned to al-‘Abbas and said, ‘O Abbas, uncle of the Messenger of God, how much of the Pleiades star remains?’” He said: The scholars claim that it appears on the horizon after falling for seven days. He said: No seven days had passed before they had rain. This is based on the question about the time in which God usually sends down rain, not that this star has an effect in itself in causing rain to fall, for this is what is forbidden to believe. Some of these hadiths have already been mentioned in the words of God Almighty: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, I think, or someone else, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man when they were receiving rain, saying: We received rain because of some of the lion’s cubs. He said: You have lied, rather it is God’s provision. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Salih al-Sarari told me, Abu Jabir Muhammad bin Abdul Malik al-Azdi told us, Ja’far bin al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No people receive rain in a night except that a people become disbelievers in the morning. Then he said: And you consider your provision to be that you lie. Someone says, We received rain because of such and such a star. And in a hadith on the authority of Abu Sa’id, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If people were to be drenched for seven years and then they received rain, they would say, ‘We received rain because of the star of al-Majda’. Mujahid said: And you make your provision that you lie. He said: Their saying about the signs, Our rain is due to such-and-such a sign, or Due to such-and-such a sign, means: Say it is from God and it is His provision. Ad-Dahhak and others said the same. Qatada said: As for Al-Hasan, he used to say: Evil is what a people have taken for themselves. They have not been provided with anything from the Book of God except denial. So the meaning of what Al-Hasan said is: And you make your portion from the Book of God that you lie about it. That is why he said before it: Is it this narration that you are deceitful? And you make your provision that you lie.

Malik said in Al-Muwatta’ from Salih ibn Kaysan from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas’ud from Zayd ibn Khalid Al-Juhani that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) led us in the dawn prayer at Al-Hudaibiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said: Do you know what your Lord has said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “He said: ‘Among My servants there have become some who believe in Me and some who disbelieve. As for he who says, “We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of God,” he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. Al-Farra’ said: None will find its taste and benefit except the one who believes in it. Others said, None shall touch it except those who are pure, meaning from major ritual impurity or ritual impurity. They said, The wording of the verse is a statement, but its meaning is a request. They said, “What is meant by the Qur’an here is the Mushaf, as Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade traveling with the Qur’an to the land of the enemy for fear that the enemy might obtain it.” They cited as evidence for that what Imam Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm that in the letter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to Amr bin Hazm that none shall touch the Qur’an except the pure. Abu Dawud narrated in Al-Marasil from the hadith of Al-Zuhri who said: I read in a document with Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: None shall touch the Qur’an except one who is pure. This is a good and reliable hadith that was read by Al-Zuhri and others, and something like this should be accepted. Ad-Daraqutni narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Hazm, Abdullah bin Umar, and Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas, and there is a problem with the chain of transmission of each of them. And God knows best. And the statement of God, A revelation from the Lord of the worlds means that this Qur’an was revealed by God, Lord of the worlds, and it is not as they say that it is magic, soothsaying, or poetry. Rather, it is the truth about which there is no doubt, and there is no beneficial truth beyond it. And the Almighty’s saying: Is it then that you are in denial of this narration? Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That is, you are denying and not believing it. Ad-Dahhak, Abu Hazra, and As-Suddi said the same. Mujahid said: In denial means you want to agree with them in it and rely on them. And you make your provision that you lie. Some of them said: The meaning of And you make your provision is your thanks that you lie, meaning you lie instead of thanks. It was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas that they read it as And you make your provision that you lie, as will come. Ibn Jarir said: It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Haytham Ibn Adi that from the language of Azdshanu’ah is what someone has been provided with meaning what someone has been thankful for. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-A'la, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: And you make your provision say, 'Your gratitude is that you lie,' and you say, 'We received rain because of such and such a star, because of such and such a star.' This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Makhul ibn Ibrahim al-Nahdi, and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, and on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Bakr, all three of them on the authority of Isra'il, with it as a marfu' hadith. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Mani', on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad who is al-Marwazi, with it as a hasan gharib hadith. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abd al-A'la, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: No people ever receive rain except that some of them become disbelievers in the morning, saying, 'We received rain because of such and such a star.'" Ibn Abbas recited: And you make your provision that you deny. This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Ibn Abbas. Malik said in Al-Muwatta’ from Salih ibn Kaysan from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas’ud from Zayd ibn Khalid Al-Juhani that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) led us in the dawn prayer at Al-Hudaibiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said: Do you know what your Lord has said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “He said: ‘Among My servants there have become some who believe in Me and some who disbelieve. As for he who says, “We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of God,” he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. As for he who says, We have been given rain because of such-and-such a star, he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i, all from the hadith of Malik. Muslim said: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi and Amr ibn Sawad told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told us, Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: “God does not send down a blessing from the sky except that a group of people disbelieve in it in the morning. Rain comes down and they say, ‘It is because of such and such a star.’” Muslim is the only one to narrate it from this chain of narration. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God may grant a people a blessing in the morning or in the evening, and some people disbelieve in it in the morning, and they say, ‘We were given rain because of such and such a star.’ Muhammad said: He is Ibn Ibrahim. I mentioned this hadith to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: “We have heard it from Abu Hurayrah, and someone told me that he witnessed ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him praying for rain. He said: No seven days had passed before they had rain. This is based on the question about the time in which God usually sends down rain, not that this star has an effect in itself in causing rain to fall, for this is what is forbidden to believe. Some of these hadiths have already been mentioned in the words of God Almighty: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, I think, or someone else, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man when they were receiving rain, saying: We received rain because of some of the lion’s cubs. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, and its answer would be: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an. Others said: The la is not redundant and has no meaning, but rather it is used at the beginning of the oath if it is sworn by something negative, like the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: No, by God, the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman. 56:83: God the Almighty says: Why then, when it reaches meaning the soul the throat meaning the larynx, and that is when death is imminent, as God the Almighty said: No! When it reaches the collarbones * And it is said, 'Who has ascended?' * And he thinks that it is the separation * And the leg is wound around the leg * To your Lord, that Day, is the driving. For this reason He said here: And you, at that time, will be looking on meaning at the dying person and what he is suffering from the throes of death And We are nearer to him than you meaning with Our angels but you do not see meaning but you will not see them, as God the Almighty said in the other verse: "And He is the Prevailing over His servants. And He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. Then they will be returned to God, their True Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners." And God the Almighty said: Why then, if you are not to be held accountable, do you not return it? meaning why do you not return this soul that has reached the throat to its original place and seat in the body if you are not to be held accountable? Ibn Abbas said: It means accountants. A similar statement was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and Abu Hazra. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Why, if you were not to be judged not believing that you would be judged, resurrected and rewarded, then return this soul. Mujahid said: Not to be judged not certain. Maymun bin Mihran said: Not to be punished, subdued.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi told us, Iyas ibn Amir told me, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When the verse So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Make it in your bowing. And when the verse Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make it in your prostration. And this is how Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Musa ibn Ayyub, and Ruh ibn Ubadah said: Hajjaj al-Sawwaf told us from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever says ‘Glory be to God, the Almighty, and with His praise,’ a palm tree will be planted for him in Paradise. This is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Ruh, and he and al-Nasa’i also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir from The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and rare. We do not know it except from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari said at the end of his book: Ahmad ibn Ashkab narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to us, Amara ibn al-Qa’qa’ narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to God and His praise, glory be to God the Almighty.” The rest of the group narrated it except Abu Dawud from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fadil with a similar chain of transmission, at the end of the interpretation of Surat al-Waqi’ah. To God be praise and thanks.
